prepareIcon takes a noun for its problems, so a profile picture is refused in its own words; the same 256 pixels square serve both (E9).

entries.plain: Notices when a workspace this computer hosts is stopped, so the app can offer to start it again.
entries.summary: Recognizes a remembered workspace hosted here that is currently stopped.
details: Matches a saved loopback address and explicit port against lastHosted; repeated workspace names are not identity.
Checks hosting phase to avoid offering resume while starting/stopping, and a failed optional status read retains normal connection behavior.

entries.plain: Keeps the screens up to date on whether this computer is hosting a workspace, and which one it hosted last.
entries.summary: Shares live native hosting status and the most recently hosted workspace.
details: useHostingStatus combines status reads and native subscriptions. A revision ensures a newer live update takes precedence over an older request result.
Refresh retains the existing status instead of blanking controls, and useLastHosted rereads after relevant hosting changes while ignoring results from a disposed effect.

entries.plain: Decides whether a huddle shows as the call or as the chat with the huddle bar, opens the call by itself when someone turns on a camera or shares a screen, and checks whether anyone's camera or screen share is on.
entries.summary: Defines the call and chat views of a huddle, when the call opens by itself, and detects visible video.
details: huddleHasVideo checks local camera/share and every peer's camera/share stream.

useHuddleView opens the call when video starts, and again when someone new starts sharing. When the video stops it goes back to the chat, unless the person opened the call themselves. Out of a huddle it is the chat.
This small presentation rule keeps screen layout independent from the WebRTC transport implementation.
ringingLine names who a call's ring still rings, Ringing Maya…, for whoever is in the call; aloneLine is that, or then, for the caller alone in it, who declined or that nobody answered (E10).

CAMERAS_HOLD (8) and CALL_HOLDS (16) are how many cameras and how many people a call holds up with (E13b): a camera costs everyone a decoder and its owner an encoder for each of them, a muted microphone nothing. bigCallLine is what a call past either tells everyone, that it can stutter and what helps, turning cameras off or muting when not talking.

entries.plain: The ringing sound of an incoming huddle, made in the browser.
entries.summary: Plays a quiet two-note chime, twice every three seconds, with Web Audio (E10).
details: startRingTone needs no sound file: sine notes with a quick start and a fade, through one gain. It gives back the function that stops it, and is silent where there is no Web Audio or the browser will not play yet, since the prompt says it all the same.

entries.plain: Reads which version of the code this app was built from, so the diagnostics report can show it.
entries.summary: Exposes source identity embedded by web and desktop builds.
details: Reads the build-time stamp safely when it exists and returns null for development/tests without one.
describeBuild renders a short revision and dirty-source indication for diagnostics so a running artifact can be compared with validation evidence.

entries.plain: Builds a report on how the app and server are running, without any message contents, for sharing when something goes wrong.
entries.summary: Constructs a previewable operating report without including message contents.
details: Reports source/protocol versions, connection status, pending-send count, huddle connection counts, notification capability and device/window information.

Owner/admin operating status adds database and attachment sizes, queue lengths, retention progress, disk space and event-loop timing. It reports quantities and failures rather than quoting queued messages or secrets.
The report filename uses time rather than a workspace/person name; copying or saving remains an explicit UI action.

Formats the device's call log line by line in UTC, and the server's call log as joins, leaves, setups passed on or dropped, and each side's report with its routes, servers, ICE state and cause in words.

entries.plain: Rolls up messages you missed while disconnected into one summary notification, shown at most every two minutes.
entries.summary: Groups replayed missed messages into an occasional notification summary.
details: Holds eligible messages by ID until replay is quiet for one second, with at most one summary every two minutes by default.
Before showing, stillNews rechecks read state, notification policy and access; deleted held messages can be dropped. This reduces a reconnect burst to a useful summary instead of many interruptions.

entries.plain: Groups a burst of change signals into one refresh, so busy lists do not reload over and over.
entries.summary: Bounds refresh work for lists receiving many invalidation signals.
details: soon merges a burst into one delayed request, or one queued refresh after a request already running. now cancels obsolete work and loads the current selection immediately.
At most one request runs and one refresh waits. stop cancels timers and owned transfers while allowing a subsequently reopened view to load again.

entries.plain: Decides which invite link to show again instead of making a new one, and says how long a link lasts and how many people it lets in.
entries.summary: Invite reuse rule plus expiry and use wording for the invite dialog (UX-43).
details: reusableInvite picks this person's newest invite that is active, unlimited and has at least a day left. describeExpiry rounds up through minutes, hours and days, so a one-day link reads 1 day.
INVITE_EXPIRY_CHOICES and INVITE_USE_CHOICES are what Change offers; DEFAULT_INVITE is a week for anyone.
onlyOnItsNetwork tells a private, link-local, carrier-grade NAT (Tailscale) or .local address, which a phone on mobile data cannot reach, from one anyone can.

entries.plain: The three ways Apps and integrations offers to start, an incoming webhook, a slash command and posting CI results, and the examples each one gives to copy.
entries.summary: Template names, test messages and copyable examples for Apps and integrations (UX-63).
details: curlExample posts WEBHOOK_EXAMPLE, the same message Send test message posts. ciExample is a GitHub Actions step that reads the webhook URL from the OWNBASE_WEBHOOK_URL repository secret and builds its JSON with jq from environment variables, so a quote in a branch name cannot break it.

commandExample is a Node service with nothing to install that checks the request's signature and timestamp as INTEGRATIONS.md describes and answers privately. appTemplates.test.ts runs it against signed, unsigned and stale requests.
commandName stores a command as the server does (no slash, lower case); suggestedAppName names the app a template makes.

entries.plain: Reads a long list a page at a time as you scroll, and reads it again quietly when something in it changes, so side panels stay up to date without a Refresh button.
entries.summary: Keeps a page-at-a-time list current: more on demand, in-place refresh from the top (UX-08).
details: PagedList keeps every page read so far. loadMore reads the next cursor; a refresh reads again from the first page until it covers as many rows as were shown, at most PAGED_REFRESH_PAGES pages, and swaps the result in at once so nothing blanks or jumps.

Refreshes go through a CoalescedLoader, so one read from the top runs at a time and a burst of signals is one read; reading more gives way to it. usePagedList starts a different list from nothing whenever its key changes.

start({ keep: true }), or usePagedList's keep option, leaves the rows shown in place until the different list's first page replaces them, and reads only that one page, so search does not flash empty between questions (UX-51).

entries.plain: Turns a filter typed into search, such as from:@sam, into a chip you can remove with one click, and says what each chip means in plain words.
entries.summary: Search filters as modifier tokens: parsing typed ones, combining them and naming them for chips (UX-51).
details: A filter is held as the modifier it adds to the query (from:sam, in:design, has:link, type:pdf, after:2026-01-01), so chips, typed modifiers and recent searches all reach the server as the same query text. filterToken reads one word with the protocol's parseSearchQuery and writes it one way; a word that cannot be read, such as a date that does not exist, is left in the field for the hints to point at.

takeFilters moves a modifier out of the field once a space follows it and the caret has left it, keeping the caret where it was in what is left; Enter takes every one. withFilter lets people, places and kinds add up, as the server ORs them, and lets a new day replace the old one on its side.

DATE_PRESETS name after: days relative to today where the reader is (after: leaves out the day it names), and filterLabel says Today or Last 7 days for them, a person by display name, and a day in the reader's own style.

entries.plain: Remembers the last conversation you had open in each account on this device.
entries.summary: Remembers the last conversation for this authenticated account on this device.
details: Uses the stable workspace/account key and validates a channel token when restoring. undefined means still loading and null means no usable memory.
Repeated writes to the same destination are avoided. A failed save costs a later navigation click and does not block chatting.

entries.plain: Remembers your ten most recent searches for each account, moving a repeated search back to the top.
entries.summary: Maintains up to ten recent searches within an account's workspace scope.
details: Validates and deduplicates query/channel entries, placing a repeated choice at the front.

A per-platform key queue spans closed and reopened dialogs so an older append cannot undo an explicit clear within that owner. Failure reports that local history is unavailable while server search remains usable.

entries.plain: Finds the links in a message that point at other messages in this workspace.
entries.summary: Lists the workspace messages a message's words link to, for their cards.
details: Reads the links Mrkdwn draws, Slack's <url|label> and <url> and bare addresses, outside code, and keeps those parseDeepLink reads as a message on an address the caller says is this workspace's.

Each message once, in the order named, and at most MAX_LINKED_MESSAGES (three, as many as a message gets link previews). A restored copy of the workspace elsewhere holds the same ids, so its links are left alone.

entries.plain: Lets each message redraw only when the people or channels it shows change, so typing elsewhere does not redraw them all.
entries.summary: Subscribes each message row only to the users and channels it actually displays.
details: Extracts author, mention, reaction and linked-channel IDs from message data, for a reply the author and mentions of the message it quotes, and for a forward the original's author, its conversation and the people it names.

usePick preserves object identity until a referenced entry changes and skips work while the source map is unchanged. Renaming an unrelated person or typing elsewhere therefore need not rerender every visible message.
Who chose each of a poll's choices counts too, so a voter the message does not otherwise name is shown by name and redraws on a rename (E6).

entries.plain: Remembers which message you chose to reply to in each conversation, until you send, cancel or choose another.
entries.summary: Holds the pending inline-reply choice per conversation and workspace connection.
details: Keyed like drafts, so a channel and each of its threads keep their own choice; one store per workspace client, so a choice never follows you to another server.
Each choice of Reply is counted, so choosing it again on the same message still brings the message box back into focus.

entries.plain: Knows how each kind of draft is kept, so the Drafts list, the message editor and the Scheduled list all read them the same way.
entries.summary: Reads draft keys and texts, and orders the drafts list.
details: draftPlace reads a draft key: a conversation's composer (its id), a thread's (conversation and first message), an unsaved edit (conversation:edit:message) or an unsaved scheduled edit (conversation:scheduled-edit:id). editDraftKey and scheduledEditDraftKey make the last two, and readEditDraft and readScheduledEditDraft read their stored text.

listDrafts gives the drafts to show, newest first by the times the replica keeps, then those with no time (kept by an earlier version) in the order they were stored. readDraftTimes reads the stored times, keeping only numbers.

entries.plain: Lets the Drafts list open a message's editor, even when the message is still scrolling into view.
entries.summary: Asks the row showing a message to open its editor, now or when it appears.
details: requestEdit opens the editor of the message's row if one is on screen; otherwise the next row for that message to appear within ten seconds takes the request, as after a jump to it. One never shown lets it go.
useEditRequest is how MessageItem listens, only for the person's own messages.

entries.plain: Says in one sentence what a restored backup would bring back into use.
entries.summary: inventorySummary for restore results.
details: Counts the sign-ins a restored copy still accepts, its scheduled messages waiting, app events not yet delivered and the app addresses it calls, for the notes after Restore from a backup and Earlier copies.

entries.plain: Shared labels for file sizes, times and conversation names, plus the colored initials used as profile pictures.
entries.summary: Centralizes byte/time labels, conversation titles and deterministic avatars.
details: Reusable Intl.DateTimeFormat instances avoid constructing a formatter for every message row. Day labels recognize Today and Yesterday in the reader's local time.

formatWhen is the one rule for times in lists (the time today, Yesterday, the weekday within six days, then the date, with the year only for another one), counted in calendar days so a day with a clock change is not miscounted; formatFull is the whole date and time a list's hint gives.
DM titles derive from other participants, and deterministic hues/initials give each account a consistent avatar without image requests.

entries.plain: Fetches the full set of emoji the first time something needs it, and tells whether a message is only a few emoji, so they can be shown large.
entries.summary: Lazily loads the emoji table, search and preferences, and detects emoji-only messages.
details: loadEmoji imports emojiSet.ts and emojiPreferences.ts once, about 46 kB compressed, and forgets a failed attempt so the next one tries again. The workspace calls it as it opens; useEmoji gives a component the kit once it has arrived.

onlyEmoji is true for a message of at most 64 characters made only of pictographs, flag letters, skin tones, keycaps and the joiners between them. MessageItem shows such a message at 32 px, as Slack and Discord do.

entries.plain: Every emoji the app offers, with the short names Slack uses for them, and the search over them.
entries.summary: Holds the generated emoji table and ranks search and colon completion.
details: Reads emojiData.json, which scripts/generate-emoji.mjs writes from @emoji-mart/data: 1,870 emoji in Slack's eight sections, each with its shortcode, other shortcodes such as thumbsup for +1, its name, keywords and five skin tones where it has them. Flags are reordered as Unicode lists them.

searchEmoji needs every typed word to match: a shortcode exactly, then a shortcode or a word of a shortcode or name starting so, then a keyword, then the word inside a shortcode. Equal matches go to what this person uses more, then to the shorter shortcode, so party finds :tada: before :partying_face:.
emojiStartingWith completes a word typed after a colon from word starts only, so :ar does not offer a heart. emojiNamed turns a full :shortcode: into its emoji, and inTone writes one in a skin tone.

entries.plain: The list of every emoji the app offers, with the names Slack uses for them, in Slack's sections.
entries.summary: Generated emoji table: shortcodes, names, keywords and skin tones by section.
details: Written by scripts/generate-emoji.mjs from @emoji-mart/data, one emoji to a line so a new version reads as a diff: its character, shortcode, name, the keywords its shortcode and name do not already say, and its five skin tones where it has them. The other shortcodes, such as thumbsup for +1, follow the sections.

Flags are put in Unicode's order rather than the data's, which sorted them by shortcode. emojiSet.ts imports it, so it travels in the chunk fetched on first use; a test checks it is what the generator writes.

entries.plain: Remembers on this device the skin tone you chose for emoji and which emoji you use most.
entries.summary: Keeps the skin tone and emoji use per device and orders the picker's first row.
details: A store per platform reads the saved choices once; a change made before the read finishes is applied on top of what was saved. It keeps the 60 most used emoji with how often and when.

frequentEmoji fills the picker's two-row Frequently used section with someone's own most used emoji, then common starters. likedBy weights search and completion by use, and a little for the starters, so a first :ta offers :tada: first.
writeEmoji gives the composer an emoji in the chosen tone and counts it. Without a platform, as in a test of one component, choices last as long as the page.

entries.plain: Offers quick choices for sending later, like this evening or tomorrow at 9:00, using your local time.
entries.summary: Builds schedule presets and labels using the device's local calendar.
details: Offers relative short delays, a still-future evening, tomorrow at 09:00 and next Monday morning.
localDateTime preserves the local clock for datetime-local fields; formatScheduleTime supplies Today/Tomorrow labels without treating a local calendar date as UTC.

reminderPresets are a reminder's choices: in 20 minutes, 1 hour and 3 hours, tomorrow morning, and next week (Monday at 9:00). formatReminderTime words a time to follow Remind me or Reminder set for (E4).

entries.plain: Offers how long to pause notifications and shows, in your local time, when they will come back.
entries.summary: Supplies notification pause durations and readable resume times.
details: Short options compute the deadline when selected, while tomorrow morning is a calendar time rather than an arbitrary twelve-hour delay.
Uses the scheduling formatter for a consistent resume label.

entries.plain: Shows keyboard shortcuts with the keys your own keyboard has, such as the Command key on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere.
entries.summary: Writes keyboard shortcuts as the person's own keyboard labels them.
details: isApple and modKey choose ⌘ on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere; shortcutLabel turns "Mod+Shift+U" into "⌘⇧U" or "Ctrl Shift U", so hints never name the wrong key.

entries.plain: The common statuses people pick and how long each usually lasts, offered in both the profile form and the quick status menu, and the words for when a status ends.
entries.summary: The statuses people set most, offered wherever a status is chosen.
details: One list of emoji and text presets shared by the profile form and quick status, so both offer the same choices.

Each preset carries how long it usually lasts (In a meeting and Out for lunch an hour, Heads down and Off sick today, On holiday until changed). statusEnd turns a Clear after choice into an end: minutes from now, or the last moment of today or of Sunday on this device's clock. statusUntil says it as until 3:41 PM, or until a day (UX-61).

entries.plain: Works out what time it is for someone else, and whether it differs from yours.
entries.summary: Formats a time of day in a person's zone and compares it with the reader's (E9).
details: timeIn writes the hour and minute in a zone as this reader writes times, keeping one formatter per zone, and gives null for a zone this device does not know. theirTime is someone's time now and whether it reads otherwise than the reader's, or null without a zone.

readerTimeZone is the account's zone, or else the device's under its current name (currentZoneName: Chromium gives India's as Asia/Calcutta). zoneLabel writes a zone with spaces. useMinute is the time now, changing as each minute starts.

entries.plain: Notices when nobody has used this window for ten minutes, so you can show as away.
entries.summary: Tells the workspace when this device goes idle and when it is used again (E9).
details: useIdleReport waits IDLE_AFTER_MS, ten minutes, without a pointer, key, wheel, touch or focus, then calls WorkspaceClient.setIdle(true), and setIdle(false) at the next use. A moving pointer restarts the wait at most once a second.
The workspace screen runs it. The server makes the account away only once every one of its devices is idle.

entries.plain: The Star and Mute choices in a conversation's menus, named for what they will do, with a notice if the workspace does not save one.
entries.summary: Builds Star/Unstar and Mute/Unmute menu items over a conversation's preferences, and reports a refusal with Try again.
details: starItem and muteItem name a choice by what it does now: Star channel, Unstar conversation, Mute channel, Unmute conversation. The sidebar row's More menu and the conversation's ⋯ menu share them.

Both save through WorkspaceClient.setChannelPrefs, so the choice shows at once, reaches the server in order with any other choice for that conversation, and reaches the account's other devices as a prefs event. saved waits until nothing for that conversation is being saved and says whether this choice was refused.

A refusal puts back what the workspace has and shows a notice with Try again, since the row that made the choice may have moved by then. Star is offered only for a conversation this account is in, on a server that keeps stars (WorkspaceState.stars), because an older one would drop it without saying so.
moveConversation puts a conversation in a section, or back with null, unstarring it; moveItems builds a menu's Move to group (E8).

entries.plain: Stops Enter from sending while you type in Japanese, Chinese or Korean or inside a code block, and keeps your typing position steady.
entries.summary: Protects input-method composition, code blocks and caret placement.
details: isImeKey checks both isComposing and key code 229, preventing Enter used to choose a Japanese/Chinese/Korean candidate from sending or navigating.
insideCodeBlock leaves Enter as a newline inside an unfinished triple-backtick block.
caretToRestore accepts a formatting/autocomplete position only if the text still matches the rewrite that produced it, so newer typing cannot be displaced by an old caret correction.

entries.plain: Shows mentions in the message box as readable names while keeping the hidden link to the right person or channel.
entries.summary: Maps stored mention tokens to the readable text a message box shows, and edits back.
details: projectMentions turns <@USER_ID>, <#CHANNEL_ID> and <!here>/<!channel>/<!everyone> into @name, #channel and @here segments. The stored string stays the only source of truth; an unresolved person or channel shows @unknown or #unknown and keeps its ID.

replaceShown applies an edit made to the readable text to the stored text. A mention the edit reaches into becomes the ordinary text of what remains of its label, so editing a name never silently redirects a mention and a typed or pasted name never acquires an ID.

shownEdit recovers the single changed range from before/after text, using the caret to settle ambiguous repeats. storedPosition/shownPosition translate selections, widening a selection inside a mention to the whole token for formatting.

entries.plain: Makes a person or channel tagged in the message box look tagged, rather than like ordinary words starting with @.
entries.summary: Draws each mention in a message box as a tag behind its name.
details: A textarea cannot style part of its text, so a layer behind the box holds the same text, invisible, with each mention segment of the box's MentionDocument wrapped in a .mention-tag span. The box is positioned above it with no background, so the tag shows through under the name.

The layer reads the box's padding and type from its computed style before each paint, so it lays text out as the box does (a touchscreen writes at 16 px), scrolls with the box, and has the same thin scrollbar, so a long message wraps at the same width. It is hidden from screen readers, which read the box, and absent while nothing is mentioned.

entries.plain: Makes the message box and the edit box show mentions as names, and lets Undo, Backspace and Delete treat each as one piece.
entries.summary: Binds a textarea to readable mentions for both the composer and the message editor.
details: The owner keeps stored text as before (drafts, sends, schedules, outbox and edit conflicts are unchanged strings); the hook supplies the shown value, converts each change event back, and restores the caret only while the shown text still matches.

Rewrites such as a completed mention, emoji or formatting go through document.execCommand(insertText) where available, so the browser's own Undo and Redo take them back. A bounded map from shown to stored text lets historyUndo/historyRedo restore mentions rather than plain names.
Backspace at a mention's end or Delete at its start selects the whole mention first, so one key removes it. Without execCommand (as in jsdom) the stored text is committed directly.

entries.plain: Remembers where you were reading in up to 100 recent threads until the app closes.
entries.summary: Keeps reading anchors for recently visited threads during this app session.
details: Stores root-specific message/offset positions by workspace address, removing the entry when the reader returns to the newest reply.
The oldest entry is evicted past 100 threads, bounding memory. Unlike channel history state, this cache lasts only for the running app.

entries.plain: Adds Back and Forward to the desktop app with Alt plus the arrow keys and the mouse's side buttons.
entries.summary: Adds desktop Back/Forward keyboard and mouse shortcuts.
details: When enabled, Alt+Left/Right and mouse side buttons call browser history.
Modified or already handled key events are left alone; listeners are removed with the component. Ordinary web browsers already supply this behavior.

entries.plain: Lets the screens change their layout the moment the window grows or shrinks.
entries.summary: Makes responsive decisions react to a changing media query.
details: Initializes from matchMedia when available and subscribes to change events.
The hook rechecks on a query change and removes its listener, keeping viewport-driven component behavior synchronized with CSS.

entries.plain: Keeps the conversation and the message box in the part of a phone's screen the keyboard leaves, and tells the bottom bar to step aside while you type.
entries.summary: Follows visualViewport where the browser does not resize the page for the keyboard, and marks the root while a keyboard is up.
details: The web client's viewport asks to be resized for the keyboard (interactive-widget=resizes-content), which Chrome on Android does. iOS Safari does not: it keeps the page its full height and slides it up under the keyboard. Rather than ask which browser it is, the hook looks at what it did: where visualViewport is more than a pixel shorter than the window and nobody has zoomed in, it sets --visual-height and --visual-top (the visible part's height and pageTop) and data-visual-viewport on the root, and theme.css then sizes and moves #root to the visible part. Anywhere else nothing is set.

data-keyboard marks the root while a field that raises a keyboard (a textarea, a text-like input or something editable) has focus and the visible part is at least 150 px shorter than the tallest the window has been at this width. The tallest starts again when the width changes, as when a phone turns. theme.css hides the bottom bar and gives its room back while the mark is there.

It listens to visualViewport's resize and scroll, and to focus moving, which it reads a frame later so going from one field to the next does not bring the bar back for a moment. It writes two attributes and two values and draws nothing again. It takes all of them away when the screen goes. toggleAttribute is always handed a boolean, since it toggles when handed undefined.

entries.plain: Lets a swipe in from the left edge of a phone's screen open the list of channels, and a swipe back close it.
entries.summary: Recognises an edge swipe to open the phone drawer, and a swipe back to close it, from passive touch listeners.
details: A swipe opening the drawer starts within 40 px of the left edge, wider than the strip Android keeps for its own Back gesture; once open, a swipe left anywhere closes it. It counts after 56 px sideways and at least twice as far across as down; a drag that goes more than 12 px up or down first is a scroll and is let go. A touch with more than one finger, or one starting in a field, is left alone.

The listeners are passive and never cancel anything, so scrolling still scrolls and a browser or system Back gesture from the very edge stays the browser's. The drawer's own transition does the moving, which theme.css stills for anyone who asked for less motion.

entries.plain: Copies text to the clipboard and only reports success once the copy really worked, with a fallback when the browser refuses.
entries.summary: Copies text and reports success only after a real clipboard operation.
details: Uses Clipboard API first, then a temporary selected textarea for ordinary HTTP LAN pages or refused clipboard permission.

The temporary field lives inside an active dialog when necessary, preserving the focus trap, and restores previous focus after removal. Per-key feedback and a short reset timer keep copy controls truthful.

entries.plain: Lets you move through suggestions with the arrow keys while you keep typing, and tells screen readers which one is picked.
entries.summary: Keeps suggestion navigation accessible while focus remains in the text field.
details: ArrowUp/Down wrap the selected suggestion and aria-activedescendant tells screen readers which option is active.
Mouse selection avoids stealing the caret. Left/Right/Home/End remain normal editing keys; only keyboard movement scrolls the active suggestion into view.

entries.plain: Moves keyboard focus into a panel when it opens and back to where you were when it closes.
entries.summary: Moves focus into an opened panel and returns it when the panel closes.
details: A heading receives focus when appropriate; visible disclosure toggles can keep it. Phone panels that cover their opener take focus instead.
Cleanup restores focus only if it stayed inside the closing panel or was lost, using message-row and drawer fallbacks when the original control is no longer focusable.

entries.plain: Makes a long message list easy to move through by keyboard, one message at a time with the arrow keys.
entries.summary: Turns a long message list into a practical keyboard navigation region.
details: Only the active message and its controls participate in sequential Tab order; arrows, Home and End move between articles, Enter enters actions and Escape returns to the message.
A MutationObserver reapplies the rule when rows or controls change without requiring the whole timeline to rerender. Pointer and reading-cursor access remain available.

entries.plain: Makes tabs behave the same everywhere, including moving between them with the arrow keys.
entries.summary: Implements consistent WAI-ARIA tab selection and keyboard movement.
details: One selected tab is a Tab stop; Left/Right wrap and Home/End select the endpoints. Each tab and the shared panel have matching IDs and labels.
Selection follows focus because these panels can show content or loading state immediately. Alt/Ctrl/Meta combinations are not intercepted.
Choosing a tab brings the panel in from that tab's side: from the right for one further along, from the left for one before.

entries.plain: The box where you type a message, add files, mention people, format text, answer a message in place and schedule it to send later.
entries.summary: Owns visible message text, attachments, mentions, formatting and scheduling intent.
details: Channel and thread composers use different draft keys. Typing updates local React text immediately and hands it to the client after a 250 ms debounce; an untouched composer can receive a restored or other-window draft without overwriting newer typing.

N03 uses layout cleanup plus capture-phase pagehide/visibility/native-close hooks to hand over the actual last visible text before persistence runs. This closes the gap where a final debounced keystroke could disappear on normal navigation or close.

Send validates content and limits, then queues through WorkspaceClient. The words remain owned until localWork acknowledges the send or recovery record, and refusal keeps an actionable notice rather than silently dropping the message.

The composer supports Unicode-aware mention suggestions, slash-command hints, emoji, formatting preview, drag/paste attachments, progress and reply broadcast choice. IME and code-block Enter rules prevent premature actions; pending caret moves are tied to the text they were computed for.

The field shows mentions as names (choosing @here shows @here) through useMentionField, while text, drafts and sends keep <!here> and <@USER_ID>. A mention already completed is not offered again; the character limit counts the stored text the server receives.

Send later's choices are TimePopover, loaded when the clock is first pressed. Scheduling uploads attachments, persists the exact request including nonce, file IDs and chosen time before posting, and restores unresolved scheduling requests before another send. A retry reuses the original request identity rather than creating a duplicate schedule.

While Reply is chosen, a bar above the text names whom you answer, with an @ toggle for whether they are notified and a close button; Escape cancels it before the panel behind can take Escape. One send answers it, and Send later is not offered meanwhile because a scheduled message cannot answer in place.

A word typed after a colon is completed from every emoji by Slack's shortcodes, the closest and most used first, in this device's skin tone; a shortcode typed out in full, as :tada:, becomes its emoji when its closing colon is typed, except in code. The emoji arrive with the kit the workspace fetches as it opens.

Since Q04 the preference caller keeps Enter a new line when the saved choice cannot be read. N03 covers normal preparation and persistence acknowledgements, not every power-loss or OS-termination case.
Send later opens TimePopover with its own presets and words.

Where the server keeps polls, the round plus opens a menu, Upload a file or Create a poll; elsewhere it attaches a file as before, and guests see neither (E6). /poll, with any words after it as the question, opens the same PollDialog, loaded on first use, and once the poll is made the /poll is cleared. A guest's /poll is answered here that guests cannot make polls.
Its box sits over MentionTags, so a mention chosen or restored from a draft reads as a tag; a name typed or pasted stays words.

entries.plain: Saves your drafts and messages waiting to send on the device, and brings them back when you return.
entries.summary: Bridges in-memory unsent work to acknowledged account-scoped storage.
details: Creates stable drafts, outbox and unstored-sends keys from authenticated workspace/account identity. Restores records strictly, then subscribes to client changes and other-window storage changes.

Tracks only this window's draft changes against confirmed base values and only its queued sends/refusals/removals with revisions. Shared merges preserve unrelated work and consume tombstones rather than resurrecting removed sends.

Outbox persistence precedes clearing corresponding durable drafts. If a send was typed and sent before a saved draft existed, a separate unstored-sends recovery record can preserve its words when the outbox write fails.

Recovery restores a nonce's words as a send or a draft according to durable ownership; missing File bytes still remain visibly unavailable. Failed reads and writes show Retry, and an ordinary retry flushes current memory instead of rereading stale disk over newer intent.

For N03's native persist phase, restoration must succeed, current changes are flushed, and all owned writes including recovery follow-up work settle. Confirmed remaining differences and a retained failure prevent a later no-op write from falsely acknowledging lost text.

Pagehide/hidden/unmount ask for immediate flush, while normal desktop close can await acknowledgement. A browser crash relies on the storage journal when available; this file cannot promise that every refused or abruptly interrupted write reached disk.

Keeps a draft-times record beside the drafts (E5): read on restore and handed to hydrateDrafts, and written after each drafts write of this window's own with the times of the drafts it wrote, pruned to the drafts stored. Only the Drafts list's order rides on it, so a read or write that fails is let go without the warning.

entries.plain: Checks that this workspace address may use your saved drafts before loading them, and asks you about a new address.
entries.summary: Keeps local-work components unmounted until the current address is admitted.
details: Reads workspace and account identity from the ready replica, then checks the local trusted-address record. The gate shows checking, explicit approval, saving or retryable error before mounting drafts/search-history consumers.
Approval explains that the address can access saved local work and may resume queued sends. Effects fence results to their current client/workspace/account scope.
The gate relies on the trust helper's answer and cannot compensate for an incorrectly admitted address; Q02 closed the helper's simultaneous first-registration gap.

While it waits it shows the workspace's banner across the top (such as sign-ins this device could not save) and, under its message, this computer's hosting line, so a hosted workspace that will not start still offers Manage hosting (UX-25).

entries.plain: Shows a form that a connected app or bot sends you, keeping its answers apart from any form that replaces it.
entries.summary: Renders an app-owned form with input and result lifetime bound to its view ID.
details: ViewModal keys AppForm by view.id, so a newly arriving app form starts with its own values, field errors, message and busy state.
Inputs are keyed by block and action ID and submitted as a nested payload. Validation refusal keeps the form open and focuses the first refused field.

E18a: selects for options, people, conversations and channels; checkboxes and radio buttons as a fieldset; several-answer pickers as a checkbox list that gains a search field past six choices, keeps chosen ones in sight and stops at the app's limit; native date and time inputs. Pickers offer what this replica can see, and a starting choice it cannot see is left out.

E18b: an app may stack forms. The footer's close goes back to the one under it (named "<label>, back to <title>" for screen readers) and the dialog's own close shuts them all; both tell the server so other devices follow. Answers are kept per view id while a form is in the stack, so going back finds them, and an update keeps what was typed and drops old errors. A view of text alone has no submit button.

N05 adds alive and submitting guards plus ID-bound client operations: a previous form's success, failure or dismissal cannot close or contaminate its replacement. Answers are not persisted locally and closing alone does not send a callback.

entries.plain: The list of messages in a channel, which loads older ones as you scroll and keeps your reading spot.
entries.summary: Shows bounded channel history while preserving reading and scroll position.
details: Loads initial, older and newer history through owned request tickets. A top visible message and offset anchor preserve position while prepending rows; explicit message jumps center and highlight a target.

Readers at the latest message stay pinned as content or viewport size changes; readers looking back are not pulled to the bottom, except by a send of their own, which brings them down to it as Discord and Slack do. History entries remember where a conversation was being read.

Separately renders optimistic pending sends with Retry/Discard and ephemeral app answers with dismissal/limit notices. Date dividers, an unread boundary and typing indicators make the timeline understandable.

Read acknowledgement follows a genuinely visible tail, and useRovingMessages makes the list a manageable keyboard region. The actual row count is bounded in client-core rather than claiming full DOM virtualization.
A waiting forward shows its card under its words, as it will once sent.
A waiting poll shows its question and choices, through PendingPoll, with nothing to press (E6).

entries.plain: Shows one message with its author, time, text, files and reactions, plus the actions you are allowed to take.
entries.summary: Renders one message and its authorized actions with narrow replica subscriptions.
details: The memoized row renders author, timestamps, mrkdwn, files, reactions, thread affordances and app buttons. useMessageReferences tracks only referenced users/channels, and self identity/role controls relevant actions.

Reaction, pin and saved toggles report refused optimistic changes through a toast with a repeatable intent. Delete uses an explicit confirmation; mark unread delegates channel or thread cursor behavior to the client.

Copying text/link waits for clipboard outcome. App link buttons navigate normally while interactive buttons call the app through the server and wait for its result; permissions remain enforced by the server.

The in-place editor is a lazy chunk with an inline loading status and a recoverable failure, keeping editing code out of the entry every visit downloads. The emoji picker for a reaction is a lazy chunk too, with a dialog that says so if it cannot load.

The editor takes the place of the words only: a message's files and its ForwardCard stay under it, since an edit changes neither. Link previews and app buttons are hidden until the edit closes, as saving can change the previews.

Reply answers a message in place (Shift leaves its author unnotified) and Reply in thread opens its thread, as in Discord; inside a thread, Reply answers one of its replies. A reply shows its quote above it through ReplyQuote, and a reply that notified you is marked as a mention is.

The hover toolbar draws its icons at 18 px with a stroke of 2, beside the reaction emoji, and marks each button icon-live so its icon moves when pointed at. A saved message's bookmark takes the accent colour alone; with two text colours on the button, the stylesheet's order had left it looking unsaved.
A message of only a few emoji (onlyEmoji in lib/emoji.ts) is shown at 32 px, as Slack and Discord show one.

Forward… (E1) sits in the menu and the toolbar's More, offered only where the server forwards and where forwardSource finds something to pass on. It opens ForwardDialog, a lazy chunk, with the source as it was when chosen. A forward shows its ForwardCard under its files.
A message's link previews show under its files through LinkPreviews, with Remove for its sender (E2).
Under the previews, LinkedMessages shows a card for each message in this workspace the words link to. Both are hidden while the message is edited.

Mute thread or Unmute thread (E3) sits in More actions and the touch menu of a thread's first message in the channel, offered where the server mutes threads, once the thread has replies or while it is muted. A muted thread's reply count shows a bell-off mark and is named "N replies, muted".

Remind me about this… (E4) sits in More actions and the touch menu where the server keeps reminders, and opens TimePopover from the row. Once set, the menu offers Change reminder… and Cancel reminder, or Mark reminder done once it is due; a toast says when it is set for, or that it was refused, with Try again.
Opens its editor when the Drafts list asks for this message's unsaved edit, through useEditRequest, for the person's own messages only (E5).
A poll's question shows in its PollCard rather than as the message's words, and Edit message is offered nowhere for a poll, nor by the Drafts list (E6).
A call's note (Message.call, E10) shows as a CallNote in place of its words, and Edit message is offered nowhere for one.

MessageItem draws a message from someone blocked as one line, Message from someone you blocked with Show, keeping its article role and data-message-id for the arrow keys and links; MessageRow is the message itself. Report message… (lazy ReportMessageDialog) is in both menus for someone else's message where the server takes reports (E12).

entries.plain: The small form for reporting a message to the workspace's admins: what is wrong with it, and anything to add.
entries.summary: Reports a message with a reason and an optional note (E12).
details: Four reasons as radio cards, each with a line on what it covers, and a note of up to REPORT_NOTE_MAX characters. Send report without a reason says so and puts focus on the first.
It says the admins will see the message, who wrote it and the report, and that its author is not told. A sent report closes the dialog with a notice; one that failed stays open and says why.

entries.plain: The box for editing a sent message, which keeps unsaved changes and refuses to overwrite a newer edit made meanwhile.
entries.summary: Edits a message while preserving unsaved words and the original comparison base.
details: An edit draft has its own message-specific slot and stores both text and the message text it began from, including compatibility with older plain-text drafts.
Save uses expectedText so a concurrent edit can be refused instead of being overwritten unnoticed. Formatting, preview, IME and code-block behavior match the composer.
The box and the Current message shown on an edit conflict read mentions as names; the kept {text, base} and the saved text keep their tokens. MessageItem loads the editor on first use.
Its draft key and the reading of a kept edit come from lib/drafts.ts, which the Drafts list shares (E5).
Its box sits over MentionTags too, so a message's mentions read as tags while it is edited.

entries.plain: The side panel that shows a thread's first message, its replies and a box to reply.
entries.summary: Displays a root message, paged replies and an independent reply composer.
details: Loads the root's thread through WorkspaceClient, displays optimistic replies and manages retry/discard for waiting sends.

Remembers reply reading anchors, protects current thread history from eviction and acknowledges the thread cursor when appropriate. Follow/Unfollow calls the client's thread-follow logic, which sends those requests in order (Q09).
A thread composer uses a root-specific draft key and optional also-send-to-channel choice rather than clobbering the channel composer.
It is a chunk of its own, fetched as the workspace opens and drawn directly from then on, which keeps the first download under its size limit.

Beside Follow, a bell-off toggle named Mute thread (aria-pressed) mutes and unmutes the thread through the client (E3), offered only where the server mutes threads. Muting turns Following back to Follow.
A waiting poll in a thread shows the same way, through PendingPoll (E6).

entries.plain: The shared layout for the Pins, Saved and Threads panels. Each keeps itself up to date while it is open and shows more as you scroll. A message can be taken out of Saved from the Saved panel itself, with Undo.
entries.summary: Shares the layout and live, scroll-to-load behavior for Pins, Saved and followed Threads.
details: The generic panel renders a PagedList of server-loaded messages with row context, loading/empty/refusal state and a LoadMore end. listKey names a different list; a change of refreshKey, or of changedContent for a conversation it shows, reads it again in place (UX-08).

Pins are channel-specific, Saved spans readable conversations, and Threads represents followed conversations with unread counts and opens the thread rather than a single message. Saved refreshes on the saved set, Threads on follow state including each thread's lastSeq, so a new reply shows at once.
Since Q08 PinsPanel also passes its channel's changedContent marker in refreshKey, so a pin, edit or deletion outside the loaded timeline is seen.

keep hides a row this device already knows no longer belongs, before the list is read again. remove gives each row one action that takes it out, shown on hover or focus and always where there is no hover, as Activity's and Drafts' are. Focus then goes to the next row's Open button, or the heading when none is left, and the row drops the second click of a double-click (dropRepeatClick), since the next row's button slides up under the pointer. SavedPanel uses both: Remove from Saved unsaves at once with an Undo notice, and a refusal puts the row back with Try again.

entries.plain: The search window, which finds words in messages and file names. Results come straight under the box, filters are chips you add from From, In, Has and Date or by typing from:@name, and more results load as you scroll.
entries.summary: Searches server-side message text and attachment names, results first, with filters as removable chips (UX-51).
details: Under the field sit the filters in force as chips, each one click to remove, then From, In and Has menus and a Date popover (Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, or a day either side) to add more; a ? button shows the modifier syntax. Typed modifiers become chips through lib/searchFilters.ts. The field and chips stay above the results, which scroll, so results start within about 90 px of the field at 1280x820.

Results follow what is typed and the filters chosen a quarter-second after typing pauses, and the previous answer stays on show while the next question is out, its status line and marked words still those of the question it answers. Enter searches at once; a search is kept among the recent ones only when someone settles on it (Enter, a recent search repeated, a result opened). Words brought from the palette are searched at once and kept. Recent searches show before anything is asked, and repeating one turns its modifiers back into chips. With none kept yet, an EmptyState says what can be searched and how to add a filter.

Messages and Files tabs: Files asks the same question with has:file (unless a filter already asks for files) and shows one row per file, marked with the words searched for. Results are read through usePagedList, 30 at a time, with LoadMore at the end instead of Previous and Next pages.

Since Q07 the results are read again in place, from the top as far as they had been read, when changedContent advances for a channel among them, leaving a read in flight to finish first and asking once more if it began before the change. Results are still a copy: after a resync beyond the event log they are stale until asked again.
inConversation opens it on the conversation it was asked from, as an In chip, from the header's menu (UX-23), without adding a recent search.

entries.plain: Lists what is new for you, everything unread, mentions or replies in threads you follow, grouped by conversation, one line each. New ones appear while it is open, and more load as you scroll.
entries.summary: Lists unread messages, mentions and followed-thread replies in groups, as a live, scroll-to-load list with coalesced refreshes.
details: Tabs All, Mentions and Threads (UX-52) ask the server's unread, mentions and threads modes; Threads shows only where the ready snapshot says activityThreads. Each tab is its own PagedList. Mention counts, edits and retention in conversations it shows, and in All and Threads each followed thread's lastSeq (All also each conversation's newest seq), signal that it may be out of date (UX-08).
A 250 ms coalesced refresh merges bursts, reads again as far as was shown and keeps existing content meanwhile.

groupActivity puts rows under one heading per conversation (per thread in Threads), in the order each group's newest came, named like "#design, 3 new"; a one-to-one DM's group is "Direct message" since its rows name the person. A row is one line (author, in a thread, time, the start of the text from notificationBody) and opens the message; Mark read reads a conversation, or a thread through markThreadRead's through, up to that row, and Save toggles saved. Mark all read reads every conversation and followed thread to its newest, and any listed reply in a thread not followed. Focus moves to the next row when the one holding it leaves.
A Reminders tab (E4), where the server keeps reminders, shows RemindersList; its name carries how many are due. All starts with a row saying how many reminders are due, which opens that tab.

entries.plain: A side panel listing your direct messages, newest first, with what is unread, so a conversation with someone is two taps away on a phone.
entries.summary: Lists the account's direct and group conversations from live state as a side panel, with unread, mention, draft and muted marks.
details: Opened by DMs in the phone's bottom bar, and at #/c/<channel>/p/dms. Like every side panel it loads on first use in LazyPanel, takes focus on its heading through usePanelFocus, and below 1024 px covers the conversation.

The list is the sidebar's own: conversations of type dm or group_dm this account is in and that are not archived, newest first by channelLastSeq. It comes from the workspace's live state, so it keeps itself current with nothing to load once the workspace has arrived; before then it shows ListStatus's stand-in rows.

Each row is a button at least 48 px tall with the first other person's avatar and presence, the conversation's name, and Draft, Muted, a red mention count or an Unread dot; the one open is marked. Choosing one opens it, which closes the panel. The header has Friends (with a dot for requests waiting) and New message, which a guest does not get. The count, the dot and Friends' dot are Badges, always drawn so one that comes while the panel is open pops in.

Empty, it says how to start one and offers New message; a guest is told direct messages are for members. While the connection is down a line says the list may be out of date, and what this device knows stays listed.
Someone away shows a ring rather than a filled dot (E9).
Leaves out a one-to-one DM with someone blocked (E12).

entries.plain: Shows the messages you scheduled to send later, including failed ones, and lets you edit, reschedule or cancel them.
entries.summary: Shows queued, held and failed schedules and lets the author resolve them.
details: Loads server-owned schedules and presents future delivery times, status and attachment context.

Supports editing/rescheduling, cancelling and returning words to the appropriate draft. Server scheduling uses request identity, while the client preserves actionable refusal state and reads the queue again after an edit it could not confirm.
It reads the queue again whenever scheduledChanges moves: the server's private scheduled event, or a new connection. Only a server without scheduledEvents is still asked every 15 seconds (UX-08).
initialEdit opens one queued message's unsaved edit once the list has it, for a draft opened from Drafts (E5).

entries.plain: Lists every message you started and left unsent on this device, and every edit you have not saved, the newest first, so you can pick one up again or throw it away.
entries.summary: Lists this device's drafts for the account, newest first, to open where they were written or delete.
details: Reads the drafts and their times from the replica, so it keeps up with typing here and with other windows on this device without loading anything. A conversation's draft, a thread's, and unsaved edits of a message or a scheduled message each say where they belong; drafts in conversations no longer here, and keys it does not know, are left out (lib/drafts.ts).

A row opens the draft where it was written, as WorkspaceScreen's openDraft does it. Delete takes it away at once, with a toast and Undo, which puts the words back with their time unless something was written there since.
Its header links to Scheduled, except for a guest, who cannot schedule.

entries.plain: The Files panel: every file shared in the conversations you can read, newest first, which you can narrow to pictures, documents or the rest, to one person or conversation, or by words in the name.
entries.summary: Lists shared files a page at a time from the server, filters them, opens or saves one and goes to the message that shared it (E7).
details: Search by name waits for typing to rest a quarter of a second. Kind is a tab row (All, Images, Documents, Other) through useTabs; From lists everyone, you marked, and In the conversations this person is in and every public channel. Opened from a conversation's menu, In starts on that conversation. Each change is another list, read from the top through usePagedList, with Show more.

A row is one button named with the file, its size, who shared it, where and when. A picture opens in the Lightbox; anything else, or a large picture, is saved through useFileDownload, which says when it fails. Beside it, Show in conversation goes to the message.

A picture's square loads once it scrolls near, at the size a message would fetch; anything else shows its kind's icon. Empty, it says nothing is shared yet, or that nothing matches with Clear filters. It reads the list again when a listed conversation's content changes, as Saved does.

entries.plain: Shows attached files as cards, loads image previews as they scroll into view, and opens them full size.
entries.summary: Displays file cards, lazy authenticated image previews and full-size lightboxes.
details: Image loading begins near the viewport using IntersectionObserver, then retains/releases the shared FileCache resource. Large or non-image files use cards and scoped download URLs instead of eager inline transfer.

A resource is bound to the active client/file and can show loading, failure, retry or invalidated state. N10 cache notices make open previews become unavailable when their owner message/thread is removed.

Pending attachments use temporary local previews; lightboxes share the modal focus layer. The UI distinguishes a failed download from successful handoff rather than claiming the browser/OS completed it.
The full-size viewer itself is Lightbox.tsx, loaded on first use behind an error boundary; this file keeps the shared useFileResource and saveUrl it reads through.
useFileDownload is FileCard's saving, taken out so the file browser saves a file the same way (E7); opensAsPicture says which files open in the viewer, a picture under the native-download size.

entries.plain: The full-size view of a picture, with Save and Close, loaded the first time a picture is opened.
entries.summary: Shows one image full size over the conversation through the shared file resource.
details: Reads the image through Attachments' useFileResource, so loading, failure, retry and a file taken away behave as in inline previews; a picture that will not decode says so and can still be saved.
Kept out of the entry every visit downloads: Attachments' Lightbox loads it on first use, shows nothing new while it loads, and says the viewer could not load if its chunk fails.

entries.plain: The list of times to pick from, for sending a message later or being reminded about one: a few times from now, or any date and time.
entries.summary: Offers a caller's presets and a custom local time, loaded when first opened.
details: Send later and reminders (E4) both choose with it. The caller names it (label, which also heads the list), gives the presets, and words the button under the field for the time chosen there or none yet.
The whole popover mounts at once, so Popover measures and places it with its real height; the custom time lives here and is cleared when it closes.
The button names the time chosen before it is used. The caller still owns the request, its recovery record and what it says once the server confirms.
The button is never greyed out: pressed with no date and time, or one already past, it says so under the field and puts focus there, and nothing reaches the caller.

entries.plain: Activity's list of messages you asked to be reminded about: those due now first, then the ones still to come, each to finish, move or cancel.
entries.summary: Lists this account's reminders under Due and Upcoming, with Done, Change and Cancel.
details: Reads GET /api/reminders, due ones first, the latest first, then waiting ones, the soonest first, and reads it again whenever this account's reminders change in the replica, here or on another device, keeping what is shown meanwhile.

A row opens its message. A due one offers Mark done and Remind me later; a waiting one Change reminder and Cancel reminder. Changing opens TimePopover from the row, and a refusal says so with Try again.
Rows in a conversation this client no longer has are left out, as Activity's other lists leave them.

entries.plain: Turns message formatting like bold, code, quotes, lists, mentions and links into what you see, and reveals where a link really goes.
entries.summary: Renders the supported Slack-style message syntax into React elements.
details: Handles fenced and inline code, bold/italic/strike, quotes, user/channel references and ordinary or labelled HTTP links without interpreting message text as arbitrary HTML.

Resolves mentions against supplied users/channels, with the same labels the composer shows (mentionDocument), and opens a message link in-place only when it belongs to a known address of this workspace (useOwnAddress, which LinkedMessages asks too).
A labelled link that looks like a different host exposes the actual destination. Code/quote edge trimming avoids artificial blank lines around block elements.

lineRuns splits text outside code blocks into text, quote, bulleted and numbered runs. Lines starting "- ", "* " or "• " become a ul, and "1. " or "1) " (up to three digits, so a year is not one) an ol that counts on from its first number, as Discord's does. "-5", "*bold*" and a bare marker stay text, and a list marker inside a quote stays in the quote.

entries.plain: The emoji picker, laid out like Slack's: the ones you use most, every emoji by section, a search, and a skin tone choice.
entries.summary: Lets someone find any emoji by section, search or keyboard, in their skin tone.
details: Marks along the top jump to Frequently used and Slack's eight sections; the grid has nine emoji to a row under sticky section titles. The footer names the emoji under the pointer or the arrows with its :shortcode:, and holds the skin tone choice.

Focus stays in the search box, a combobox, and a screen reader follows the choice through aria-activedescendant. Up and Down move a row, into the next section where one ends; Left and Right move one emoji once the arrows are in the grid or nothing is typed; Enter picks.

Sections out of view are held open at their exact height and drawn when scrolling, a jump or the arrows come near, so opening it does not make all 1,870 emoji. Each section draws again only when the choice moves in or out of it or the tone changes.
Section marks are Its Hover's and Lucide's drawings; THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md credits them.

entries.plain: The formatting buttons and shortcuts, such as bold and italic, shared by the message box and the edit box, plus the length limit.
entries.summary: Shares formatting transformations, shortcuts and message length limits.
details: formatText wraps or inserts syntax and returns the corresponding selection so composer/editor behavior stays consistent.

formatList makes each line the selection touches a bulleted or numbered item (numbered from 1), changes items of the other kind, or takes the markers off when every line already has that kind's; a caret keeps its place in its line's words. listShortcut reads Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+8 and +7 from the key's code, as Shift changes the key, and the toolbar has a button for each.
The toolbar supplies supported formatting and preview affordances; formattingShortcut and MESSAGE_LIMIT keep keyboard handling and validation aligned.

Its emoji button opens the same EmojiPicker the reactions use, loaded on first use, with a loading line meanwhile and a message if it cannot load. Escape, its own button or a press anywhere outside it closes it, and a press outside leaves focus where it landed.

entries.plain: Where you pick an emoji to react to a message with, or for your status, hanging off what it is for, or as its own window on a touchscreen.
entries.summary: Places the shared emoji picker beside a message or the status emoji button, or in a dialog on touch.
details: Shows EmojiPicker in a Popover anchored to the message with a pointer, and in a Dialog on a touchscreen, and closes as the reaction is sent.
Touch users tap before opening the software keyboard, allowing the picker to show choices without the keyboard immediately covering them.

Kept out of the entry every visit downloads: MessageItem loads it the first time someone asks for more than the toolbar's three reactions, shows nothing new while it loads, and says the picker could not load if its chunk fails.
ProfileForm opens it, titled Choose a status emoji and lined up with the button's start, to choose a status's one emoji; a pick replaces the one there.

entries.plain: The line above a reply showing who wrote the message it answers and how that message began, as Discord draws it.
entries.summary: Renders an inline reply's quote and leads back to the original.
details: A curved line runs from the reply's avatar to the original author's small avatar, name and a one-line excerpt with mentions shown as names and formatting marks left out.

Clicking it is handled by the message row: an original on screen is scrolled to and briefly lit, and one that is not is opened by the same jump search and links use. A deleted original says so and opens nothing.

entries.plain: The box under a forwarded message that shows the message it passes on: who wrote it, when, what it said and its files.
entries.summary: Renders a forward's card and leads back to the original where the reader can open it.
details: The header names where the original was said, #name for a channel and the people for a DM. A card from a private conversation forwarded elsewhere says only that, and a deleted original says so. Neither shows an author, words or files.

View original opens the message through OpenMessageContext. It is offered only when the reader's replica has the original's conversation and the original is not deleted, and not in ForwardDialog's preview, where it would open the message behind the dialog.

conversationName is shared with ForwardDialog, so the list and the card name a conversation the same way. MessageItem imports the card directly, so it is in the entry bundle; the dialog is a lazy chunk.

QuotedMessage, the author, time, words and files, is shared with LinkedMessages, so a forward and a linked message read the same; the linked one gives its time with formatWhen, since it can be from any day.

entries.plain: The window for forwarding a message: pick where it goes, add a few words if you like, and see what the others will see.
entries.summary: Chooses a conversation and an optional comment, previews the card and sends the forward.
details: The list holds the conversations the person is in and every public channel, since posting joins one. Typing filters it by name, at most eight rows show, and useListbox drives it as in the switcher. Enter picks the active row.

MessageItem passes a ForwardSource: the message itself, or the original of a forward with no words or files of its own. The preview is forwardOf for the chosen conversation, so it hides a private original going elsewhere as the server will.
Forward goes through client.send, so the forward waits in the outbox like any message. Without a conversation it asks where and focuses the field; a full outbox keeps the dialog open and says why.

entries.plain: The boxes under a message that preview the web pages it links to: the site, the page's title, a short description and its picture.
entries.summary: Renders a message's link previews, with their server-fetched pictures and Remove for the sender (E2).
details: Each card names the site, links the title to the page (only an http or https address becomes a link, opened in a new tab without a referrer), and shows up to three lines of description.

The picture comes from the server through FileCache under previewImageKey, never from the site. One at least 400 pixels wide and wider than 1.3 to 1 sits under the words in a box of its own proportions, so nothing jumps while it loads; a smaller one is a 72 pixel square beside them. A picture that cannot be loaded leaves nothing.
The sender sees Remove on each card, which calls WorkspaceClient.removeLinkPreview and says so in a toast if the server refuses.

entries.plain: The box under a message that links to another message in the workspace, showing who wrote that message, when, what it says and where, as Slack does.
entries.summary: Shows each message a message links to in a card, read as the reader may see it now.
details: linkedMessages picks the links (at most three, each once, none in code) and drops one to the message itself. Each card says Posted in #name, or in a thread, or in a direct message with whom, then QuotedMessage, then View message, which opens it through OpenMessageContext.

useLinkedMessage uses the copy this device holds in a timeline or a loaded thread, so an edit shows as it is made. Otherwise it asks getMessage, once per message for each value of changedContent for its conversation, and keeps the last answer up while it asks again, so the card does not blink and stays while offline.

Each reader asks for their own copy, so a message from a private conversation shows only to its members and nothing is asked about a conversation missing from the replica. A 404, deleted or out of reach, shows no card, and neither does a message from someone this account blocked.

entries.plain: The poll in a message: the question, each answer with a bar for how many chose it and their faces, and Close poll for the person who asked.
entries.summary: Renders a poll from shownPoll, votes by pressing an answer, shows a closed poll's result and lets its author close it (E6).
details: Each answer is a button with aria-pressed, named by its words, its count and who chose it. Pressing one votes for it at once, moving a single-choice vote, and pressing it again takes it back. A refused vote goes back and a toast says so.

The bar is the answer's share of the people who voted, so a poll taking many choices can add up past 100%. Up to three faces show who chose it, and its name lists them with "you" last, as a reaction's does, unless the poll is anonymous; then nobody is named, the person's own choice included only for them.
A closed poll, or one in an archived conversation, shows its rows as plain text, the person's own choice said in words. Close poll asks first, through useConfirm, since votes are final after it.
PendingPoll shows a poll still sending, its question and choices with nothing to press. MessageItem imports the card directly, so it is in the entry bundle; PollDialog is a lazy chunk.

entries.plain: The line a missed call leaves in a direct message, with a way to call back.
entries.summary: Shows a call's note (Message.call) in place of its words: a huddle nobody answered (E10).
details: Everyone but the caller reads Missed huddle with Call back, or Join huddle while the huddle is still going, and nothing to press while in it here; the caller reads No answer. Calling back joins through useCallPreferences, so it rings the others again.

entries.plain: The window for making a poll: the question, two to ten answers, and whether people may pick more than one and whether who picked what stays hidden.
entries.summary: Collects a poll's question, choices and rules, says what is missing beside the field, and sends it through the outbox (E6).
details: Enter in the question moves to the first choice; Enter in a choice moves to the next, and in the last filled one adds another, up to ten. Remove choice is offered while there are more than two.
Create poll checks before sending: a question, at least two choices and no two the same, ignoring case. Each problem is said beside its field, which takes focus.
It goes through client.send with poll, into the conversation or thread it was opened from; a full outbox keeps the window open and says why.

entries.plain: The small window for naming a sidebar section, new or renamed.
entries.summary: Takes a section's name, says what is wrong beside it, and stays open with the reason if the server refuses (E8).
details: One field, up to SIDEBAR_SECTION_NAME_MAX characters. An empty name is asked for again; otherwise it waits for the caller's answer, which is null once the server has the name or the reason it refused.
The sidebar loads it on first use, for New section... in a row's menu (the row then moves into the new section) and Rename section... in a section's menu.

entries.plain: The sidebar with your workspaces, starred conversations, channels, direct messages, unread marks and account menu.
entries.summary: Combines workspace switching, conversation navigation, unread context and account actions.
details: A compact workspace rail and workspace menu expose remembered workspaces without presenting saved tokens to the visible navigation.
Channel and DM rows show unread/muted/activity state and choose destinations supplied by the workspace screen. Admin actions appear only where the current account can use them.
Snooze controls compute actual resume times and use the client's latest-choice behavior. Menu grouping saves vertical space so short windows retain room for conversations.

A guest's sidebar leaves out Friends, Scheduled, New channel and direct messages, says Guest under the name, and offers Create an account in place of invites and account settings. Once the guest has posted, KeepAccountOffer sits above the account panel (UX-44).

A channel's row ends with Discord's two buttons while it is pointed at, holds the keyboard, or is open: invite and settings. Invite on a public channel opens the workspace's invite, since everyone in the workspace is in every public channel, and only for someone who may invite; on a private one it is Add people, which opens the channel's Members tab, for someone channelPermissions lets invite. The gear opens the channel's details, opening the channel first if it is not the one on screen. The buttons sit beside the row's button, not in it, and on a touchscreen show on the open channel only.

HostingStatus is this computer's hosting, under the workspace's name and its connection line (UX-25): a dot for live, starting or stopping, or trouble, what it is doing or what is wrong, and Manage (named Manage hosting for a screen reader). A warning is an alert. It replaced a bar along the bottom of the window, and leaves out the workspace's name when the hosted workspace is the one on screen. The storage gate's waiting screen shows it too.

AccountMenu is exported for the phone's bottom bar, which opens the same menu from its own You button by passing trigger (its label, class and content); the menu then rises as a sheet on a touch phone. The sidebar's own trigger is unchanged.

The account menu opens with AccountHeading, whose menu it is: your picture with whether you are here, your name and your @handle (Guest for a guest). In the sidebar it is 256 px wide, wider than its trigger. A status that is set shows under Clear status, with until when, in a group named Status; Keyboard shortcuts shows the keys that open the sheet; Diagnostics has a dial (gauge).

Starred (UX-20) sits above Channels once something is starred, and goes when nothing is. A starred channel or direct message moves out of its usual section, as in Slack, and keeps its unread, mention, draft and muted marks. Starred lists by name, channels and people together, so a row stays where it was put rather than moving each time a message arrives. It folds away like Channels and Direct messages and is remembered on this device with them. An archived channel leaves it with its star kept, and comes back to it if the channel is brought back.

Every conversation's row ends with More (⋯), after invite and settings on a channel's: Star or Unstar, offered only where the server keeps stars, and Mute or Unmute, each named by what it does now. A right-click on the row, or the keyboard's menu key, opens the same menu. The row's buttons stay shown while the menu is open (data-menu-open), so the menu has a place to sit and focus a place to come back to. A row starred or unstarred from its own menu changes section, and focus follows it to its More button there, or to the header of a folded section it went into.
The workspace menu offers Workspace settings to the owner and admins, after People and Apps; members and guests do not see it (UX-60).

The rail draws each workspace through WorkspaceIcon: the one on screen with useCurrentWorkspaceIcon, the other saved sign-ins with the copy this device kept (OtherWorkspace.icon), each falling back to its square (UX-60).

Its counts are Badges: Activity a red count of mentions or a quiet one of unread conversations, Threads a quiet count of threads with unread replies, a row's red mention count named with its channel, and a dot on a section's header button (Friends) for what is new. The rail's own badge is still CountBadge.
Activity's red badge counts due reminders with unread mentions, named for what it counts (E4).

A Drafts row under Saved opens the Drafts panel, with a quiet count of the drafts it lists (E5). It shows only while there are drafts or the panel is open, so an empty row does not take a channel's place beside Getting started (UX-20).

A Files row under Saved is there while the file browser is open, as Drafts is, so it costs no channel's place beside Getting started (UX-20); onFiles is given only where the server lists shared files (E7).

Sidebar sections (E8): the account's sections sit between Starred and Channels in their order, each listing its conversations by name, channels and people together; a conversation naming a section the account no longer has goes back where it would be. An empty one says how to fill it. A section folds like the others, kept on this device as section:<id>. Its header menu renames it (SectionNameDialog, lazy), moves it up or down where it can go, and deletes it after asking.
