A row's menu has a Move to group (each other section, New section..., Remove from), and a row can be dragged with a pointer onto a section, Starred, or its own Channels or Direct messages; the place lights while it would take the row, and nothing happens where it already is. Focus follows a moved row, as it does a starred one.

Away (E9): on a server with profiles the account menu has Set yourself away, or Set yourself active once away by hand, and its heading and the footer show away as a ring; a direct message's row rings the dot of someone away.

A one-to-one DM with someone blocked is left out, with its unread uncounted. The workspace menu offers Reported messages to admins on a server that takes reports, with how many wait as its hint, and its trigger shows a dot and says the count (E12).

entries.plain: On a phone, a bar along the bottom of the screen with Home, DMs, Activity and You, so the places people look for most are in sight. It also lets a swipe in from the left edge open the list of channels, and keeps the screen clear of the on-screen keyboard.
entries.summary: The phone's bottom navigation bar, the edge swipe that opens the drawer, and the on-screen keyboard handling, for the web client.
details: The bar shows at the width half of theme.css's drawer query (760 px and narrower), so on a phone held upright; on its side a phone keeps the drawer alone, since height is what it lacks there. The web client only: the desktop app's window is never a phone. It is a nav named Main navigation, each place a button 56 px tall with an icon and its label, the one you are in marked with aria-current.

Home goes back to the conversation from a panel, and from the conversation opens the drawer with every channel, as a tab bar's current tab goes to its top. DMs opens the Direct messages panel and Activity the Activity panel; both cover the conversation and stop above the bar, so moving between them is one tap. You opens the sidebar's AccountMenu from its own button, as a sheet on a touch phone. A guest has no DMs, so the bar has three places.

Badges count what waits elsewhere, as the drawer's button does: the conversation on screen and muted ones do not count. Home has a dot for unread channels, DMs a red count of unread conversations, Activity a red count of mentions or a dot for unread replies in followed threads. Each is also said in words, as the button's description. They are small Badges, 16 px and capped at 99+, hidden from a screen reader since the description says them.

The bar is inert under the open drawer, which covers it. useEdgeSwipe opens the drawer while theme.css's drawer query matches and no dialog is open; useOnScreenKeyboard runs on every size, so the layout follows the keyboard on a phone on its side too.
With the drawer closed, the sidebar's heading, the workspace's name, is hidden with it, so a visually hidden copy stays the page's h1, in a top-level header (the page's banner).
Activity's count in the bar adds due reminders to mentions, and says both (E4).
A DM with someone blocked does not count as unread (E12).

entries.plain: The Ctrl+K box for jumping to a channel, a direct message or a person.
entries.summary: Provides Ctrl+K navigation to channels, DMs and people.
details: Builds labelled suggestion rows and keeps text-field focus with useListbox; IME Enter stays text input.
Existing conversations navigate directly, while a person without a DM starts one and shows pending/failure state. This is a navigation convenience over the server-authorized openDm operation.
It is kept out of the entry every visit downloads and fetched as soon as the workspace opens; see WorkspaceScreen.

entries.plain: The side panel listing who is in a conversation, grouped by who is online.
entries.summary: Shows the active conversation's people grouped by online presence.
details: DMs use their known participant IDs; channels fetch membership when opened and ignore results after disposal.
Active users are sorted by name, grouped online/offline and linked to profiles. Shared loading and focus helpers make failure/retry and dismissal consistent.
A channel's list is asked for again, in place, when someone joins or leaves (memberChanges).
Someone away (E9) is listed among those here with a ring for a dot, and says Away under their name when they have no status.

entries.plain: The channel settings window for its topic and description, its members and managers, and your notifications for it.
entries.summary: Edits channel details and manages membership, managers and notification choices.
details: Presents topic/description and member controls under shared channel permission rules; the server remains responsible for enforcement.
Updates, inviting/removing members, changing managers and leaving map API refusals into readable actions. Channel notification writes expose retry rather than silently abandoning a refused choice.
Opens on About, or on Members (initialTab) when Add people on a private channel's row in the sidebar opens it.
The Notifications tab's not-saved notice speaks for the notify level and muting only. A star that was not saved says so where it was chosen.

About's Save changes is never off until something changes. The name and topic are TextFields. Sent with no name it says so under the name and puts the cursor there; a name another channel has comes back under the name too, and other refusals go in the alert at the top. Sent unchanged, it writes nothing, so the channel's members are not sent the same details again: a quiet status line says there is nothing to save, and says Saved after a save.

entries.plain: Windows for making and browsing channels, starting a direct message and turning a guest into an account.
entries.summary: Groups channel creation/browsing, new conversations and guest account forms.
details: NewChannelDialog creates public/private channels; BrowseChannelsDialog lists and joins available channels; NewDmDialog chooses participants and opens a direct/group conversation.

These occasional forms are lazy-loaded by the workspace screen rather than required for every returning conversation view. Invite people moved to InviteDialog.tsx, so its QR encoder loads with it alone.

GuestAccountDialog keeps a guest's identity as an account; the new session token reopens the workspace as the same person. Its Username and Password are TextFields checked on submit with the server's rules (2 to 32 lowercase letters, digits, . _ or -, and at least 8 characters): the button is never off until filled in, each problem is said under its field, the first gets focus, and a taken username comes back under the username.
Browse channels and New message say an empty or filtered-out list with EmptyState; New message's sits after its list of people rather than inside it.

entries.plain: The Invite people window. It opens with a link ready to copy, a QR code for phones, and a way to make a link that lasts longer or lets fewer people in.
entries.summary: Invite people: a link ready on opening, inline length and use limits, QR code, and the list of codes (UX-43).
details: On opening it shows the newest invite this person made that still works like a new one, or makes one for seven days and any number of people, so there is no generate step and opening it again does not mint another code.

Change makes a new link from Expires after and Number of uses, two small Selects. Copy link confirms with a toast as well as on the button; the QR code is left out when the only address reaches this computer alone.
It lists invites with their status and lets the creator or an administrator revoke one after a confirmation. Clipboard outcome and readable server refusal state are preserved.

With welcome it is the step that ends founding a workspace (UX-42): titled Invite your people, it leaves out the list, ends with Done, and says when the link only works on its own network, pointing a desktop host to Manage, under the workspace's name, to share the workspace on the internet.

entries.plain: Draws a QR code for a link on this device, dark on white in either theme, so a phone camera can open it.
entries.summary: Renders a QR code as one SVG path with a quiet zone, using the uqr encoder.
details: Encodes with error correction level M, which survives about 15 percent of the code being smudged or covered, and keeps the four-module quiet zone scanners need.
Nothing leaves the device: the encoder runs in the page, never through a service.
TwoStepSettings draws an authenticator app's otpauth URI with it (E11).

entries.plain: Shows someone's profile with a way to message them, and lets you edit your own name, status, picture and time zone.
entries.summary: Displays a person's profile and provides the shared self-profile editor.
details: ProfileForm updates the current user's name and status through Api. Another person's profile can start/open a direct message.
A status's emoji is a button that opens ReactionPicker, loaded the first time it is pressed, rather than a text box, so a status holds one emoji; a pick replaces it.
Since Q11 a press on Message is dropped once the card closes or shows someone else, so a late answer neither navigates nor changes the card.

Your own form offers Clear after (30 minutes, 1 hour, Today, This week, Don't clear) once there is a status; a preset picks its usual length, and a status saved again keeps the end it was set with. Someone else's card says until when their status lasts (UX-61).
A profile says Active now, Away (a ring, E9) or Offline, and the person's local time where their zone is known, with the zone, written with spaces, where their clock reads otherwise than yours.

Your own form, on a server with profiles (E9), uploads, changes or removes a picture through prepareIcon, and chooses a time zone from the device's list under current names, offering this device's own with Use it; each saves as it is chosen.
Block <name> asks first, through the shared confirmation where there is one, saying what blocking does; once blocked the card says so and offers Unblock, and no friend actions (E12).

entries.plain: What stands in for the message box in a direct message with someone blocked, and the list of blocked people in Account settings.
entries.summary: BlockedComposer and BlockedPeople, both with Unblock (E12).
details: BlockedComposer takes the composer's place in a one-to-one DM with someone blocked: it says so, and Unblock brings the composer back. BlockedPeople lists everyone blocked under Security, each with Unblock, and says when there is nobody; it is absent where the server does not block.
Both unblock through setBlocked and say when that did not work.

entries.plain: The other person's time of day beside a direct message's name, when it is not yours.
entries.summary: Shows the one other person's local time in a direct message's header where their clock reads otherwise (E9).
details: Only with exactly one other person, whose time zone is known; nothing when their time reads as the reader's. useMinute changes it as each minute starts.
The workspace screen puts it after the topic in a direct message's header.

entries.plain: Lists your friends in the workspace and lets you send, accept or remove friend requests.
entries.summary: Lists contacts and friend-request actions within the workspace.
details: FriendActions requests, accepts or removes a relationship through Api and displays current request state.
The list resolves workspace people and supports opening their profiles or conversations; relationship state belongs to the server-backed replica.
An empty tab says so with EmptyState: no friends yet, no pending requests or no people found.
Someone away shows a ring for a dot (E9).

entries.plain: Account settings, with sections for your profile, notifications, appearance, calls, security, devices and storage, a search that goes straight to a setting, and a quiet "Saved" when a choice is kept.
entries.summary: A settings window of account, device and presentation settings in routable sections.
details: Section keyboard navigation and route callbacks connect profile, notifications, appearance, composing, calls, security, devices and storage to Back/Forward history.

Drawn in SettingsWindow, a window over the workspace like the other dialogs, which it shares with Workspace settings. It gives the window its search field, what the search found, and the open section's content.

The search lists matching settings from settingsSearch in place of the sections. Enter or a click opens the setting's section, scrolls the setting to the middle, focuses its control (or its heading) and marks it briefly for anyone who sees no focus ring. Escape in a filled search clears it; the next one closes the window. A setting whose label sits above its field, as Select and TextField draw it, is marked together with its field.

Choices that save themselves report through savedNote, and the section's title row says "Saved" for two seconds in a polite live region that is always present, so it is read out without competing with the section's own status messages.

Uses shared preference stores for notification preview, Enter behavior, appearance and join-muted choice. Calls includes a local microphone check and N04 retry for unreadable call preferences. When I press Enter is a Select.
Security and Devices change passwords, list/revoke sessions and sign out through the server; Storage displays server usage. Confirmation identifies destructive session changes.
The Q03 and Q04 repairs live in the underlying helpers; this dialog only shows their state, including Try again for a composer preference that could not be read.
Security holds TwoStepSettings between Change password and Sign out (E11).
Security lists blocked people after two-step sign-in (E12).

entries.plain: The part of Account settings, under Security, where someone turns on two-step sign-in with an authenticator app, keeps their recovery codes, and turns it off.
entries.summary: Sets two-step sign-in up and manages it, a step at a time (E11).
details: Setting up takes the password, then shows a QrCode of the otpauth URI and the key in fours with Copy key, then takes a first code in a one-time-code field. The ten recovery codes then show once, with Copy codes, Save as a file (a text file through a download link, as Diagnostics saves its report) and Done; their panel takes focus.

Once on, it says how many recovery codes are left, in the alert colour at three or fewer, and offers New recovery codes and Turn off, each after the password. A setup that took too long goes back to the password and says so.
Each step's field takes focus as it shows, and a password field always starts empty. Guests, who have no password, are not shown it.

entries.plain: The part of Account settings, under Security, where someone links their company sign-in to their account, or unlinks it.
entries.summary: Linking an account to the workspace's single sign-on (P9).
details: It shows for each sign-in method with a connect path in server-info, says whether this account is linked and as whom, and offers Link or Unlink. Guests and workspaces without single sign-on see nothing.

Link asks the server for a one-time path and opens it in a new tab or the system's browser, so this window stays signed in; it asks again when the window has focus back. Only a path on the workspace's own server is opened.

entries.plain: Workspace settings, where the workspace's owner and admins rename it and choose who may join, with a quiet "Saved" when a choice is kept.
entries.summary: A settings window for the workspace's own name and join policy, for its owner and admins (UX-60).
details: Drawn in the same SettingsWindow as Account settings, its sections (General, Who can join) on the left as tabs and the open one on the right. It loads on first use, so it adds nothing to the entry chunk.

General has the workspace's name in a TextField with Save. Save is never disabled: sent empty or with a tab or line break, the field says what is wrong and takes the cursor; a server refusal lands under the field too. While nothing is typed, a rename made elsewhere replaces what the field shows.

Who can join is a radio group of the three policies, each with a plain explanation, saved the moment one is chosen through WorkspaceClient.setAccessPolicy. The title row says "Saved" for two seconds through savedNote. A failed change shows what the server has and says why.

While guests are allowed a line says that choosing either other rule signs every guest out. When guests have joined, leaving guest_allowed asks first with useConfirm, since signed-out guests have to join again.

When this desktop app hosts the workspace on screen (hostedHere), Who can join says that Open to all in Manage hosting chooses who can join for the public link, and that Manage hosting shows and changes the same setting while the link is open.
On a server without ReadySnapshot.workspaceSettings it shows the name, offers neither control, and says the workspace is changed where it is hosted.

General starts with the workspace icon (UX-60): the current icon or its square, Upload icon, which opens a hidden file input from the keyboard or a touch, and Remove, which asks nothing since uploading again puts it back. A chosen picture goes through prepareIcon and WorkspaceClient.setWorkspaceIcon at once, says Saved, and a refusal is said under the buttons, described by Upload icon, which takes focus. Neither button is ever disabled; aria-disabled marks one while its request runs. A server without ReadySnapshot.workspaceIcon gets no icon part.

General ends with Link previews (E2): one checkbox, saved the moment it changes through WorkspaceClient.setLinkPreviews, with a plain note that the server reads pages so no device contacts the site, that private addresses are never read, and that turning it off keeps previews already shown. A server without previews leaves it out.

entries.plain: Draws the settings that the server's add-ons, such as single sign-on, put in Workspace settings, and saves them.
entries.summary: Generic settings panels from the server's extensions (P9).
details: useExtensionPanels() reads GET /api/admin/extension-settings for the owner; Workspace settings adds its Sign-in section only when there is a panel. An older server has no such route and shows nothing.

Each panel is a form of text, url, secret and toggle fields with its problem and status lines; Save sends every field to the panel's own path, except a secret left empty, which keeps the one saved, then reads the panels again.

entries.plain: The window Account settings and Workspace settings open in, with the list of sections on the left and the open section on the right.
entries.summary: The shared frame of both settings: name, sections as tabs, the open section's title row and one scrolling region, on Modal.
details: Where there is room it is a window over the dimmed workspace, 880 by 680 px at most, styled and animated like the other dialogs, with one close button in its corner. Every section opens in the same size of window, so choosing another moves nothing under the pointer.

On the left, on the sidebar's colour: the settings' name, whose they are, an optional search and the sections as a tablist that the arrow keys, Home and End move through. On the right the section's name and the "Saved" note stay in sight while the section scrolls in a DialogScroll under them.

Each section gets its own scroller, keyed by section, so it opens at its start, and the edge fade follows its own content. Chromium otherwise keeps the fade a scrolled section ended on when the next one has nothing to scroll.
A newly chosen section steps in from the side of the list it is on (stepIn). In the desktop app the backdrop starts under the 40 px title bar so the window controls stay usable.

Below 57rem wide, on a phone or in a narrow window, it fills the screen on the conversation's colour, and the sections become a strip that scrolls sideways and brings the chosen one to its middle. The rules are in theme.css.

entries.plain: Draws a workspace's picture: its icon when it has one, and otherwise its own coloured square with its first letter.
entries.summary: One part for the workspace icon or its gradient square, everywhere a workspace is shown (UX-60).
details: Takes the workspace's name, an optional object or data URL, a size in pixels, and classes for its rounding and letter size. With an image it is an img with an empty alt; without one, the workspaceGradient square with one initial, or two in the rail.
Always aria-hidden, since the workspace's name is beside it or on the control holding it. A picture that fails to load falls back to the square.
Used by the rail in Sidebar, the saved, served and resumable rows and the join card in JoinScreen, both of Manage hosting's views in HostDialog, and Workspace settings' preview.

entries.plain: Lets admins see everyone's account, find someone by name, and change roles, deactivate people, reset passwords or hand over ownership.
entries.summary: Lets administrators inspect accounts and manage access under server role rules.
details: Lists the workspace's users from the store, which an admin's snapshot holds in full and user.joined/user.updated keep current, so there is no Refresh. listAllUsers adds only last-seen times; if it fails the rows still show and ListStatus offers Try again. Someone whose presence leaves online while it is open shows as last seen then, and a change made here is applied from the server's answer before the socket's copy arrives.

A search field matches name or handle as the switcher does (a leading @ ignored); deactivated matches are counted under the list rather than hidden silently, and Escape empties the search before closing. Offers role/deactivation/invite-permission actions, password reset and ownership transfer where permitted.

PersonMenu consolidates row actions into one accessible menu. Confirmations and mapped refusal messages communicate lost access, protected ownership and equal-admin restrictions; hidden buttons are not treated as authorization.

Transfer ownership asks for the new owner's username in a TextField and checks it when pressed: missing or typed differently, it says so under the field and puts focus there. While the change is saved the field is read-only and the button aria-disabled.
Reset two-step sign-in is in a person's menu only when the admin list says they have it, and asks first (E11). The list's twoStep is kept as the socket brings changes to people.

entries.plain: Where the workspace's admins see the messages people reported, and dismiss them, remove the message or deactivate whoever wrote it.
entries.summary: The admins' queue of reported messages (E12).
details: Each reported message shows its author, where and when it was posted (a DM by its members' names), its words through readableText, or that its author deleted it, and every report of it with the reporter, the reason and the note.

Dismiss acts at once; Remove message and Remove and deactivate ask first. Deactivation is offered only where People would allow it: not oneself, not the owner, another admin only for the owner. The list asks again whenever openReports moves, so another admin's settling shows.

entries.plain: Where bots and other connected apps are set up and managed, along with their slash commands and delivery status.
entries.summary: Manages bot apps, webhooks, commands, subscriptions and callback configuration.
details: Creates and removes integrations and exposes explicit credential replacement actions. Bot tokens shown once stay only in this UI session; rereadable secrets have reveal/copy controls.
Configures slash commands, event subscriptions and verified interactivity URLs; refreshes composer command hints when those change.
Delivery status distinguishes waiting, given-up and never-queued events and offers retry where supported.

Scopes (E18c): the create form has a What it may do disclosure (ScopePicker, posting only by default, as are template apps); each app's card has the same picker, saved as ticked through setAppScopes and taken back on failure (AppScopes); each subscription names the scopes its events are waiting on, from eventScopes and APP_EVENT_TYPES, with an Allow button. Scope names are shown beside plain words, since an app's own instructions name them. Nothing about scopes shows for a server before them.

It opens on templates (UX-63): Incoming webhook, Slash command and Post CI results, as tabs sharing one choice of app (a new one or an existing one) and channel, so a webhook made in one is ready in another. A webhook template makes the app and webhook in one click, fills its URL into the example and posts the example's message to the URL itself (postToWebhook). The command template adds the command, fills the app's signing secret into the example service (dotted out on screen, copied whole) and runs /command test in a chosen channel, showing the server's reason when the app fails. Each template's row is small Selects (Channel, Post as) and small TextFields (New app name, Command, Request URL), from the same classes as the app's own forms below.
OAuth, Socket Mode, scopes, ts and the link to the published integration contract are folded into How this differs from Slack.

Each app's Slash commands, Event subscriptions and Interactivity forms are fieldsets named by their legend, with small TextFields (Command, Request URL, Description). Their buttons are never off until filled in: sent empty, a form says what is missing under each field and focuses the first, and a request in flight is only aria-disabled. A refused event or interactivity address is said under the field. Saving the interactivity address works unchanged too, rechecking it, and says Saved and verified, or that buttons are off when it is empty.

entries.plain: Shows a page-by-page history of admin changes, written as readable sentences.
entries.summary: Shows paged administrator changes as readable audit sentences.
details: Looks up current names from stored IDs and defensively interprets details, so newer or partial records remain understandable.
Loads only when requested, pages through the server audit log and preserves keyboard focus when the final page removes a pagination control.
Renaming the workspace and changing who can join read as sentences too, with the old and new name, or the new rule in plain words; an entry made by the desktop app's host names the host.
Says workspace.icon_changed as changing or removing the workspace's icon (UX-60).
Says workspace.link_previews_changed as turning link previews on or off (E2).
Says user.two_step_reset as turning off someone's two-step sign-in, and account.recovered adds that the host turned it off when it did (E11).
Says report.resolved as dismissing a report, or removing a message after reports, with how many (E12).

entries.plain: In the desktop app, starts and stops the workspace you host and handles its folder, backups, who may join and outside access.
entries.summary: Controls desktop hosting, workspace folders, backup/restore and public reachability.
details: A stopped workspace in the list offers Earlier copies, which opens EarlierCopies under its row; the result goes in the list's note. A row's name keeps at least 12rem, so its buttons go to the next line before it narrows, and its links wrap between labels.
The browser does not own a server; native Platform.hosting provides the operations this dialog presents. Existing workspace folders and new workspace names are separate start intents.
Presents running/stopped/startup status, port and rename controls, LAN and public-address choices, connector failure and launch recovery actions.
Lists hosted workspaces and backup schedules, supports backup/restore and explains a restored copy's pending apps, schedules, deliveries and sessions before activation.

N11/N12 fixes live in the desktop registry/controller: restored safety holds survive damaged metadata and cleanup ownership gates reopening. The dialog exposes those statuses; Q12 and Q13 closed the startup and queue gaps in the desktop main process, not in this dialog.

Who may join is two choices, Require an account to join and, under it, Require an invite link; clearing the first lets visitors join as guests. Before opening the choice travels with openToAll; while open it is applied with setAccessPolicy and shown as the workspace acknowledges it.

A running workspace is managed in tabs (UX-62): Overview (name with a Live pill, its network and public addresses with Copy and a QR code, who is connected, and Invite people, or Open it when another workspace is on screen), Share on the internet (plain words, then the public link card and the call relay), Backups (last backup, Back up now, the schedule) and Advanced (start-up, data folder, port). A tab shows only where this app can do what it holds. Stop hosting stays in the footer under every tab and stops without asking.

Rename and Change port, edited in place in the list, never grey out Save: an empty name or a port that is not one is said under the field with the cursor put back, a refusal from the app lands there too, and the name or port it has already just closes the form, since there is nothing to save. Your own address is a small form whose Save is off only when the environment fixes the address: sent empty with none saved it asks for one under the field, and sent unchanged it says there is nothing to save rather than saving again, because saving an address also turns invites back on. A button waiting on its request is aria-disabled, so focus stays on it.

Shows workspace icons (UX-60): the running workspace's beside its name in the overview, following HostingStatus.iconVersion, and each stopped one's in Hosted on this computer, read from its own database through hosting.icon without starting it. A missing folder shows the square.

entries.plain: The hosting card that sets up a relay so calls work between people on different networks, and tests that it answers.
entries.summary: The Calls from other networks card in Manage hosting: no relay, Cloudflare, or another TURN server.
details: Shows the saved relay without its secret; a token or password left empty keeps the saved one for the same key or username. Save reaches calls that start afterwards.

Test asks the app for the relay servers a call would be given and runs probeRelay, saying whether the relay works, refused the password, or could not be reached. A refusal calls found out about since is shown as an alert.

Save and Test are never off for want of a change. Both first check the app's own rules (a key ID of letters, digits, - and _, a token unless one is kept for that key, turn: or turns: addresses, at most eight, a username, a password unless one is kept, no spaces in any) and say each problem under its field, with focus on the first. A refusal from the app names its field by its words (Cloudflare refusing the token lands under API token); one about no field, such as the key store being locked, is an alert under the buttons. Saving what is already saved saves it again, which hands it to running workspaces afresh and replaces a saved relay that could not be read. Fields are read-only, not disabled, while a request runs.

entries.plain: Keeps the workspace's best address ready, so copying a link is instant and points somewhere others can reach.
entries.summary: Keeps known workspace addresses ready before the user copies a link.
details: Combines server-info, native hosting status and explicitly trusted aliases to choose a sharing address without awaiting a network request in the clipboard click handler.
Rechecks after reconnect, foreground return and periodically while open so temporary/public addresses can refresh. Context also tells Mrkdwn which workspace message links can navigate in-place.

useOwnAddress turns those addresses into one stable check, so Mrkdwn opening a link here and LinkedMessages showing its card agree on which links are this workspace's. Outside the provider only the connected address counts.

entries.plain: A short setup card above the channels: how many steps are left, the next one to do (create a channel, invite someone, turn on notifications, try a huddle), and All steps to see the rest. Steps tick themselves off.
entries.summary: Shows setup steps that complete from actual workspace/account behavior.
details: Tracks creating a channel, inviting someone, enabling notifications and participating in a huddle, with account/workspace-local dismissal memory.
The checklist can disappear after completion or explicit dismissal. N04's screen wiring makes its huddle action use the preference-aware join operation.

Kept short so six channels stay in sight at 1280 by 720 with it open (UX-20): one header line with the title, the count and Hide; the progress bar beside an All steps disclosure (named Show all steps, with aria-expanded and aria-controls); and only the first step still to do, as the same one-press row. All steps lists every step, done ones struck through; it is remembered with the dismissal and huddle memory, and opening it brings the rows in as a reopened sidebar category does (rows-in).

entries.plain: A small card in a guest's sidebar, shown after their first message, offering to keep them as an account with their name, their messages and a place in private conversations.
entries.summary: Offers a guest the keep-account form once, after the server has accepted their first message.
details: A guest has posted once the replica holds a message of theirs: only the server's copy reaches a timeline or a thread, while one still sending or failed waits in pending. A guest who posted before the card existed is found the same way, and the first sighting is stored, so a reload offers it even where that message is not loaded.

Not now, or Keep this account, puts it away for that account on this device: stored per workspace and account like the setup checklist, and remembered by the page as well, so a save that fails does not bring it back before a reload. Storage that cannot be read means it is not offered at all, since an earlier Not now cannot be ruled out; the menus still have Create an account.

Keep this account opens the same form as Create an account in the menus. The card sits above the account panel, so the channel list does not move when it appears, and its width is contained, so its words never widen the sidebar; it takes no focus and makes no announcement, and focus inside it when it is put away goes to the account button. It goes as soon as the guest is a member.

entries.plain: A banner asking to turn on browser notifications, which waits two weeks before asking again if you pick Not now.
entries.summary: Requests browser notification permission from an intentional visible gesture.
details: Appears after sign-in rather than asking from an unrelated first click. Not now defers the banner for two weeks on this device.
An explicit browser denial remains quiet until site permission changes, and the native desktop notification adapter does not need this banner.
It sits in the workspace's one banner place and gives way to anything more pressing (UX-25). onShowing tells the workspace whether it is on show, so the Opening message… hint behind it waits.

entries.plain: Tells the owner and admins when the workspace has more members than its plan includes, with a link to a bigger plan.
entries.summary: The member notice banner and the hook and sentence Workspace settings shares with it (P5).
details: usePlanMembers gives the plan's notice and the live member count, only to the owner and admins, so someone joining shows it at once.
MemberNoticeBanner is a status in the one banner place, after the ask to turn on notifications and a message being opened; Not now puts it away on this device for two weeks, per workspace.
The sentence names the plan when the host gave a name, and See plans opens the host's address in the browser; Workspace settings > General > Plan says the same while it is true.

entries.plain: Shows the owner and admins what the server needs them to know, such as an Enterprise license running out.
entries.summary: ServerNoticeBanner: the snapshot's server notices, one at a time, in the banner place (P6).
details: Only the owner and admins see them. An alert, such as a license that has ended, can be dismissed until the app opens again; a status can be put away for two weeks on this device.
It comes after the ask to turn on notifications and before the plan's member notice, which waits while it shows.

entries.plain: Reads out new messages to screen reader users without moving focus, grouping bursts so they are not flooded.
entries.summary: Politely announces new visible messages without flooding a screen reader.
details: A single arrival includes a bounded excerpt; a burst groups count and up to a few sender names after a quiet period.
Announcements do not steal focus, and navigation clears old-conversation waiting messages so they are not announced in the new destination.

entries.plain: The button at the top of a conversation that starts a huddle, joins one in progress or shows you are in it.
entries.summary: Header control that starts a huddle, joins the running one, or says you are in it.
details: Names the action by the room's state (Start a huddle, Join the huddle (n), In huddle) and joins through the same preference-aware path as other entry points. The In huddle dot is still: an animation that never ends had the whole call drawn sixty times a second for as long as it lasted (E13b).

entries.plain: The prompt that appears when someone calls you in a direct message, with Join and Decline, and its ring.
entries.summary: Shows each ring of a direct message's huddle that rings this account, rings, and tells the system while the window is behind (E10).
details: A card per ring at the top of the window: the caller's picture, <name> is calling, and Huddle with you or with the group's names; on a phone its buttons take a row of their own. Join opens the conversation and joins through useCallPreferences, so the device check still comes first; Decline calls WorkspaceClient.declineRing.

While it rings, startRingTone plays and a system notification says who is calling once per ring if the window is not in front, worded by ringContent; both stay quiet during Do Not Disturb and in a muted conversation, where the card still shows. The title is an alert, so it is read as it appears.
A ring from someone blocked never shows or sounds (E12).

entries.plain: The parts of a conversation's header besides its name: a search field, the faces of who is in it, the menu with everything else, and the line that says how many messages are pinned.
entries.summary: The search field, member faces and count, the conversation's ⋯ menu, and the pinned line under the header.
details: ConversationSearch is a button drawn as a field, "Search #name", that opens search on this conversation with the conversation as a filter. It takes up to 240 px, less in a narrow window, and a phone shows its magnifier alone.

MemberStack shows up to three faces, people online first, and a count; it opens and closes the Members panel. A group message knows its people; a channel's are asked for, and asked again when memberChanges moves or the connection comes back. A phone shows one face.

ConversationMenu holds Pinned messages, Star or Unstar ("channel", or "conversation" for people), Notification settings (the details' Notifications tab, only for a member) and the details. Star shows only for a member, on a server that keeps stars.

PinnedBar asks for one pin and the total, shows "3 pinned" with the newest pin's first words, and opens the Pinned panel; it asks again when changedContent moves, so a pin, an unpin or an edit shows at once. A server too old to count says only "Pinned".
The last answers are kept per client, so going back to a conversation shows its faces and pins at once instead of the header moving as they arrive.
ConversationMenu offers Files where the server lists shared files: the file browser, started in this conversation (E7).

entries.plain: One row in the place for banners under a conversation's header: what happened, and what can be done about it.
entries.summary: The banner row (alert or status) and its actions, for the workspace's one banner place (UX-25).
details: Banner takes a tone, its words and optional actions at its end. An alert is tinted and read out at once by a screen reader; a status is a quiet passing note.
BannerAction is a button whose words underline on hover, as a link would, such as Dismiss or Retry saving.
Which banner shows is WorkspaceScreen's choice, one at a time. App builds the one for sign-ins this device could not save, which the storage gate also shows while the workspace is not open yet.

entries.plain: The call bar showing who is in the huddle, who is speaking, each person's volume and anyone you cannot connect to.
entries.summary: Shows call presence, speaking rings and the header join/start control.
details: HuddleFace resolves participants and speaking state, while the compact bar hosts the controls and Show call, which opens the call, video or not.

While the call shows, the bar is hidden and keeps only HuddleAudio mounted, in the same place, so moving between the views never starts anyone's voice again, and there is one set of controls (and one screen picker) at a time.

The list of who is there (Everyone in the huddle) gives each of the others a PersonVolume row, and someone sharing a screen with its sound a second row for that sound. Someone muted for you is said to be, ahead of talking, with a crossed speaker on their face. The bar hands everyone's volume to HuddleAudio.
HuddleButton starts or joins through the shared call-preference store and provides meaningful error state. N04 makes this header path agree with Getting started about mute initialization.
Once a peer's connection has a diagnosed trouble, the bar says Can't connect to them and offers Why? See the call log.
Its line says Ringing <names>… while the caller is alone, then who declined or No answer, and adds · Ringing <names>… beside those who are there (E10).

A call past CAMERAS_HOLD cameras or CALL_HOLDS people tells everyone once, in a notice that goes by itself (BigCallNotice, a heads-up Toast, E13b), and again only after it shrinks and grows. The bar holds it because it stays mounted for the whole huddle, behind the call too.

entries.plain: The mute, camera, screen share and leave buttons, with menus to switch microphone, speaker or camera.
entries.summary: Provides shared microphone, camera, screen-share and leave actions.
details: Used by the bar and by the call, which gives them its own look (stage): squarer buttons lit from within and a solid red Leave, as Discord draws a voice channel's, drawn in ink so they read on Onyx's black and White's grey alike. Over the call in full screen (overlay) they leave out the device menus.
While the connection to the workspace is down (status reconnecting or connecting), a polite status line says the call goes on while it comes back.
Stable accessible names plus aria-pressed describe toggles; captureFailure distinguishes a cancelled picker from a permission/device problem. A lost microphone exposes retry.

Beside Mute and Camera, a small arrow opens a menu of microphones and speakers, or cameras, with the chosen one ticked (menuitemradio) and a link to Voice & video settings. The menus are left out of the full-screen overlay, because menus open on the page beneath a fullscreen element.

In the desktop app, Share screen opens ScreenShareDialog rather than asking the browser; a browser shows its own picker, and stopping needs none. Whether the picker is open is one small store for the window: the controls out of full screen draw it, in the bar or the call; in full screen they leave full screen first, since a dialog does not show over it, and draw it once full screen has ended. Moving between the bar and the call keeps it open; it closes when the huddle ends.

entries.plain: The desktop app's screen picker, like Discord's: tabs for windows and screens, a live picture of each, the resolution and frame rate to share at, and whether your computer's sound goes too.
entries.summary: Picks a window or screen to share, and how sharp and smooth, in the app rather than a system dialog.
details: Windows come first and none is chosen for you, since the window on top is usually OwnBase itself and one chosen for you could be one nobody was meant to see; the Screens tab starts on the first screen, and a list with no window opens on it. Tiles are radio buttons in a radiogroup; a double click or Enter shares at once.

The last list shows at once where there has been one (platform.screenShare.sources with quick), then a fresh one, then again every 3 s while open, so pictures move and windows come and go; a chosen window that closes leaves Share asking for another. Only a first fresh list that fails with nothing shown says so, with Try again.

Share is never off for want of a choice. Pressed with nothing chosen, an alert beside the list says what is needed and focus goes to the first tile, without choosing it: choose a window, that window has closed, the list is still being found, or (with no window listed) open one or share a screen, with focus on the Screens tab. When the list failed, focus goes to Try again. The words follow the list as it changes, and choosing a tile or another tab takes them away. A window that closed between choosing and sharing is said there too.

Share names the choice to the main process, then asks the huddle for a screen at the quality chosen (720p or 1080p; 15, 30 or 60 fps, kept on the device as screen-share-quality). A refusal from the system is said in the footer, and the dialog stays open; chosen here, even a plain refusal says sharing could not start.

Where this computer can share a screen's sound (platform.screenShare.sound, Windows on the desktop app), a Share sound switch sits beside the quality bars. It is on unless turned off, which is kept on the device as screen-share-sound, and while on the line under the tabs says everyone also hears the computer's sound. Share hands the choice to the main process with the source and to the huddle.

entries.plain: Plays everyone's voice in a call, and the sound of a shared screen, through your chosen speaker at the volume you set, even with the video hidden.
entries.summary: Keeps each remote microphone playing independently of video layout.
details: Peer audio elements attach microphone streams even when the call has no camera or the video stage is hidden.
Playback refusal produces a recovery action; one user gesture retries blocked peers while already audible streams are left intact. This avoids duplicate audio from video elements.
Each peer's audio element plays through the speaker chosen in Voice & video settings.

Each person plays as loud as you chose. Up to 100% the element's own volume does it, so the usual path is untouched. Past 100% their stream goes through a Web Audio gain into a stream the same element plays, so the chosen speaker still applies. A second, muted element holds their stream meanwhile, since Chromium gives an audio graph silence from a call's stream that no element plays (measured: 0 without it).
A boost's graph that will not start without a gesture is reported like a refused play, so Turn on sound starts it.
A share's sound plays in an element of its own beside its sharer's voice, keyed by screenSoundKey, with its own volume and the same playback recovery, so muting either leaves the other.

entries.plain: One person's volume control in a call, with a mute just for you and a slider up to 200 percent.
entries.summary: One person's volume in a call: mute for you, and a slider from silent to 200%.
details: A toggle button (aria-pressed) mutes the person for you alone, and a range input in steps of 5 sets their volume, with a tick at 100% from a datalist and the percent beside it, or Off.
Moving the slider unmutes them, since it means wanting to hear them. Used in the bar's list of who is there and inside a stage tile.
With screen, the same control sets the sound of the screen they share, kept under screenSoundKey and named as their screen.

entries.plain: The call itself, laid out like a Discord voice channel: everyone as a tile, a shared screen large with everyone else in a row under it, the controls along the bottom, and full screen for the share alone.
entries.summary: Draws the call: gallery, spotlight with a row of people, presenting, and full screen.
details: stageItems prioritizes screen shares then participants; bestFit tries column counts to find the largest 16:9 tiles for the actual container dimensions.
Video surfaces stay muted because HuddleAudio owns voices. Local self-video and remote camera/share streams display without opening a second media capture.
Resize observation updates layout, and accessible tiles/actions expose focus, fullscreen and share controls. Lazy loading keeps the call out of initial conversation downloads until needed.

It takes the conversation's column in the theme's colours (black in Onyx; White's grey with a white tile for each person) and goes dark in full screen in either theme (.call-dark): beside the chat on a wide window (the chat prop, with Chat in its header), over it otherwise. The header says where the call is and who is on the main view, with a LIVE badge for a share, and has Grid view, Chat and Hide call. The bottom bar holds HuddleControls, with Everyone else (the row under a spotlight) and Full screen beside them, or up in the header below 600 px wide.

Full screen (the button, or a double-click on the main view) shows the main view out to the screen's edges. The header and the controls float over it and step aside after 3 s without movement; keyboard focus keeps them, the focus a click leaves does not. Everyone else starts hidden there. Escape leaves full screen, since the desktop app does not on its own.

Another person's tile, in the gallery or the main view, has a volume button beside Pin. Its PersonVolume opens inside the tile rather than as a popover, because popovers portal to the page beneath a fullscreen element. A tile says when its person is muted for you. A shared screen that sends its sound has a volume button too, for that sound alone, and its tile says it is with sound, with a speaker, or that its sound is muted for you. Your own share's panel says everyone can see and hear it.
Its header says who the call's ring still rings, and alone, for the caller, who declined or that nobody answered, after the conversation's name (E10).

Each tile tells the stage how tall it draws someone else's camera or share (ReportDrawn), with the camera off too, and useCallViews gathers them once per render, in device pixels, for WorkspaceClient.setCallViews: nothing while the document is hidden, and nothing once the call closes (E13b). Names and buttons over a video are not blurred, since a blur over a video is drawn again at every one of its frames.

entries.plain: Lets you hear and see how your microphone sounds before a huddle, without sending anything to anyone.
entries.summary: Lets the user test local microphone level before joining a huddle.
details: Opens the chosen microphone with the chosen processing through client-core's testMicrophone, the strong noise filter included, so what plays back is what a call would send; if the filter cannot start it says the browser's own suppression is standing in. It shows the microphone's name and level, and opens it again when the choice changes; autoStart listens at once, as the first-huddle question does. An optional playback sends the voice to the chosen speaker.
Nothing is sent to peers or the server. Stopping the check or closing settings stops the captured tracks.

Where the desktop app opened the microphone itself (Windows, none of the browser's processing chosen), it says the microphone is heard as other apps hear it, with any sound effects set up in Windows. It reads the platform without insisting on one, so it still stands alone.

entries.plain: The Voice & video settings, where you pick devices, set noise suppression and test your microphone, speaker and camera.
entries.summary: The Voice & video section of Account settings: devices, processing and tests.
details: Microphone, speaker (where setSinkId exists) and camera pickers with the system default first; a chosen device that is unplugged stays listed as such. Changes apply to a huddle in progress through chooseDevices and are kept for every workspace on this device.

Noise suppression as Strong, Standard or Off (Discord's choice; Strong unless chosen otherwise, and Off for anyone who had turned suppression off), echo cancellation and automatic volume switches, a microphone test with playback, a two-tone speaker test, a mirrored camera preview, and join-muted. When the browser keeps device names back it offers to ask for the microphone once.
In Account settings it leaves out its own heading (titled={false}), since the window already names the section, and reports kept device and join-muted choices through savedNote.

entries.plain: Lists the backups of a stopped workspace and puts an earlier one back in its place, after asking.
entries.summary: Restores an earlier copy over a stopped hosted workspace (O01).
details: Reads hosting.backups for the workspace: its backups in its backup folder, newest first, with when each was made and its size; a copy that failed its check says so and cannot be chosen. Choose a backup folder asks the system's dialog instead.

Restoring asks first, saying that what the workspace holds now is moved to a folder beside it, not deleted, and that the copy does not start until it is put back in use. hosting.restoreOver does it; the note names where the old data went and, through inventorySummary, what the copy brings back into use.

entries.plain: Asks once, before your first huddle, which microphone and camera to use when you have more than one.
entries.summary: Asks once, before a first huddle, which microphone and camera to use.
details: callPreferences.joinHuddle asks when this device has not been asked (devicesChecked), nothing is chosen, and the browser lists more than one microphone or camera; a browser that keeps names back lists none, so it is asked on the first join after it gives them. Choosing a microphone or camera in settings counts as an answer.

The dialog, loaded on first use from WorkspaceScreen, listens through MicrophoneCheck and shows the camera through CameraPreview at once. Join huddle keeps the choice and joins with it; Cancel, or the workspace closing, joins nothing and asks again next time. Only a dialog that went without an answer calls the waiting join off.

entries.plain: Shows the full diagnostics report, call logs included, so you can read it before copying or saving it.
entries.summary: Shows the complete diagnostics report before copying or downloading it.
details: Reads server-info and optional owner/admin operating status, recording a readable failure when either is unavailable.
The person can inspect the report and choose copy or local text-file save; the dialog does not send diagnostics to another service.
The report includes this device's call log and, for the owner and admins, the server's call log, with people named by handle. Opened from a call that cannot connect, it starts at the call log.

entries.plain: A searchable list of keyboard shortcuts that follows your Enter to send setting.
entries.summary: Lists and filters keyboard shortcuts using the current composing preference.
details: Writing-key descriptions change with Enter-to-send so the help reflects active behavior.
A query matches words across keys and explanations, exposing navigation, message, formatting and call shortcuts without requiring the reader to memorize them.
Each key is drawn with the shared Kbd keycap.

entries.plain: Draws each person's picture, or their colored initials, and the dot that shows whether they are here.
entries.summary: Draws consistent avatars, with a profile picture where there is one, and presence indicators.
details: Avatar shows the person's profile picture once the client's AvatarCache has it (E9), and otherwise the account's deterministic hue and display-name initials; missing users receive a fallback. It stays hidden from screen readers, since the name is always written beside it.

PresenceDot and AvatarWithPresence draw online state with a ring matching the parent surface, keeping the same visual rule across rows and calls. Away is a ring of the same green, as Slack draws it (E9).

entries.plain: The app's set of small icons, drawn directly so nothing extra has to download. Six of them move when you point at their button.
entries.summary: Provides the application's small inline SVG icon vocabulary.
details: IconName maps to shared vector paths, stroke/size conventions and accessible usage supplied by parent controls.
Inline vectors avoid an icon font, extra network fetch and a large icon runtime dependency while keeping common controls visually consistent.

Six icons (smile, reply, thread, bookmark, edit and the three dots) are redrawn after Its Hover's and kept as named parts. Such an icon carries data-icon and each path data-part, and every part has a path length of 1, so the stylesheet can move or draw one part without a motion library in the bundle.
home (a house) and messages (two speech bubbles) are the phone's bottom bar's Home and DMs.
star (five points) is Star and Unstar in a conversation's menus.
forward (an arrow passing a message on) is Forward in a message's menu.
poll (bars of different lengths off an axis) is Create a poll in the composer's + menu (E6).
phoneOff (a handset crossed out) is Decline on an incoming huddle, and phoneMissed (a handset with a cross) marks a missed huddle's note (E10).
flag reports a message and ban marks someone blocked (E12).

entries.plain: OwnBase's logo on the Join screen: the little pixel cabin at dusk whose orange window is your server.
entries.summary: Draws the app icon inline from its generated pixel paths.
details: Renders brandMark.json on a 32-pixel viewBox with crisp edges, the same colours in both themes; at 32 or 64 pixels every pixel is whole.
Its own module, imported only by JoinScreen, so the drawing's paths load with that screen's chunk instead of the entry every visit downloads.

entries.plain: The logo's pixels, one shape per colour, written by a script rather than by hand.
entries.summary: Generated [fill, path] pairs for BrandMark, from scripts/icon-art.mjs.
details: scripts/generate-palette.mjs writes it from the same drawing as the favicons and the desktop icons; theme.test.ts fails when it differs from what that writes. Prettier skips it.

entries.plain: The app's standard buttons, in main, secondary, danger and quiet styles.
entries.summary: Centralizes primary, secondary, danger and quiet action styling.
details: buttonClass lets existing native buttons reuse variants; Button forwards native attributes and ref.
Preserves native button semantics, including form submission unless type=button is explicitly chosen.

entries.plain: A button that shows only an icon. It cannot be made without a name, which a screen reader says and which appears as its hint.
entries.summary: The shared icon-only button: a required label used as accessible name and tooltip.
details: The label prop is required by its type and becomes both aria-label and the Tooltip's text; keys adds a shortcut to the tooltip. It takes an Icon name or other non-text children.
Two sizes: regular is 32 px (size-8) for dialogs, panels and headers, small is 24 px (size-6), the smallest target axe's target-size rule accepts. round draws a circle for one on a chip.

Unlike Button it defaults to type=button, since an icon rarely sends a form. It forwards its ref through Tooltip's ref merge and passes aria-pressed, aria-expanded and aria-haspopup through, tinting while pressed or expanded.

entries.plain: A text box with its name above it and, under it, a line on what to enter or what is wrong. It also holds the one set of styles every text box uses.
entries.summary: Labelled input with hint and error wiring, and the single source of field classes.
details: TextField draws a visible label tied by htmlFor, then the input, then an error (role=alert, with an icon) and a hint. aria-describedby lists the error first, then the hint, then any the caller passes; aria-invalid is set only while there is an error. Its ref reaches the input, so a form checked on submit can put the cursor in the first field with a problem.

inputClass(size, extra) returns the classes for small (a row of fields in a card), regular (dialogs and settings) and large (the sign-in card, with field-spot). Each size is a whole set, because two utilities for one property are settled by Tailwind's order rather than the class list's. aria-invalid:border-alert turns any of them red.
inputCls is the regular size, for an input, textarea or select still drawn by hand; it used to live in Dialog.tsx, with a second copy in JoinScreen.

Field draws the label, the error and the hint around whatever control it is given, and hands that control its id, aria-invalid and aria-describedby to spread. TextField and Select are both a Field around their control, so the two read and look alike in one form.

entries.plain: A drop-down choice with its name above it and, under it, a line on what to choose or what is wrong, drawn like a text box of the same size.
entries.summary: Labelled select with hint and error wiring, drawn from TextField's classes (UX-14).
details: A Field around a native select, so its label, hint and error are TextField's: a visible label tied by htmlFor, an error (role=alert) read first, then the hint, then any aria-describedby the caller passes; aria-invalid only while there is an error. Its ref reaches the select, so a form can move focus to it. The options are its children.

The label sits above the select rather than around it. A label wrapped round a select holds every option's text too, so the field was named "When I press Enter Send the message" in Account settings, and Post as in Apps' templates read its options with its name.

Its classes are inputClass(size, selectClassName), small, regular or large, the same as a text field's, so a select beside a text field in a row lines up with it. It moved Apps' local SelectField (Post as, Channel), Invite's Expires after and Number of uses, and Account settings' When I press Enter.

Selects still drawn by hand, each for a reason: Invite's address in links has no visible label and sits in a row of its own; Profile's Clear after has its label beside it; ViewModal's app-defined fields share one label, hint and error layout with its inputs and text areas; Voice and video's device selects are named by the heading above them; HostDialog's two are not moved yet.

entries.plain: Draws one keyboard key as a small keycap, as the shortcuts list shows them.
entries.summary: The shared keycap style for a key.
details: A kbd element with a raised face and a deeper lower edge; a shortcut of several keys is several side by side. It passes its props through and adds any classes given.
Keyboard shortcuts uses it. The plain shortcut hints in the quick switcher, the sidebar's Jump to button and a tooltip's bubble keep their own quieter styles.

entries.plain: The layer under every dialog, menu and full-size image, which keeps the keyboard inside the top one and returns focus on close.
entries.summary: Owns the shared stack of modal portals and keyboard/focus isolation.
details: Tracks the active layer, makes the page and older portals inert, and permits only the top layer to handle Escape, outside dismissal and tab containment.

Focus restoration follows connected usable openers and fallback owners even if an underlying dialog was removed. Layout registration accounts for child autoFocus occurring before portal ownership is fully installed.
Central ownership avoids competing independent focus traps for dialogs, menus and lightboxes.

A dialog's scrolling region (.dialog-scroll) is a part of it, so keys pressed elsewhere in it would scroll nothing. Page Up and Page Down from outside the region, and the arrow, Home and End keys from the dialog element itself, scroll the region. Text areas, selects and modified keys are left alone.

A dialog, menu or popover leaves as it came. When it closes, a copy of it, inert, hidden from screen readers and stripped of ids, names and roles, is put where it was and plays the reverse of its opening animation, then removes itself. One closed while still opening, as a loading placeholder is, leaves nothing, and neither does anything when less motion is asked for.

A press on the backdrop that closes the layer cancels the mousedown's default. Focus goes back to the opener as the layer closes, and the press's own focus change would otherwise move it straight on to the page.

entries.plain: The standard dialog frame. Its title and close button stay in sight while what is under them scrolls.
entries.summary: Adds standard dialog structure and one scrolling region on top of Modal.
details: Supplies a titled surface, accessible description relationship, close affordance and configurable width.

The title row is fixed and the content scrolls in DialogScroll. A dialog that sets ownScroll places that region itself, between the parts it keeps in sight: a search field, the list of settings sections, or the buttons that finish a form.

The scrolling content takes its width from a container around the scroller, so a scrollbar appearing does not shift it, and it fades at an edge only while there is more to scroll to there. Both are stylesheet rules, with a plain edge where scroll timelines are unsupported.

entries.plain: A small panel that opens beside the button that opened it, such as the choices for Send later.
entries.summary: A small panel anchored to the control that opened it, such as Send later's choices.
details: Built on the modal layer like Menu: Escape or a press outside closes it, the page beneath waits, and focus returns to the control. It sits above the control, or below when there is no room, and follows it as the page scrolls.
side: "below" asks for the other way round, for a control at the top of what it changes, such as search's Date filter (UX-51).

entries.plain: The compact menu used for message and workspace actions, which works by keyboard as well as by mouse.
entries.summary: Provides one accessible compact menu for row and workspace actions.
details: Built on the modal layer, with arrow navigation, Enter selection, Escape/outside dismissal and focus return to the trigger.
Repositions with scrolling instead of abandoning an action when a live timeline shifts. Destructive and disabled items keep consistent presentation.

It grows from the corner nearest its trigger, which depends on whether it opened below or above it. With sheet set, on a touch phone (wantsSheet, read once as it opens) it is a Sheet instead: its header and its items are two cards along the bottom of the screen, and the items grow to 48 px for a finger.
Ticked items are menuitemradio, one of a set, unless the menu is multiple: then each is a menuitemcheckbox, as search's From and Has filters are (UX-51).

A heading, such as the account menu's name and picture, sits atop the items in a dropdown and a sheet alike, only to look at, since the trigger already names it. An item can have a description, a quieter line under its label, and keys, drawn as small keycaps after it in a dropdown (not in a sheet) and said with aria-keyshortcuts. An emoji takes a line icon's 16 px square at 13 px, since a colour emoji draws larger and heavier than its size.

The first item has focus as the menu opens, for the keyboard, but is drawn as chosen only once the pointer or an arrow key has been on the items (engaged), or where :focus-visible shows it after a key opened the menu. Opened with a click, nothing looks picked before it is.

Its button stays the same element for the menu's whole life, so focus has somewhere to go back to. A button with a hint used to be swapped for a bare one while the menu was open, to keep the hint away: the modal layer then found the button it remembered detached, and focus fell to the page on Escape, Tab or a choice. The hint now stays on the button, turned off with Tooltip's disabled while the menu is open.

entries.plain: The panel that rises from the bottom of a phone's screen, within reach of a thumb, with the page dimmed behind it. A tap on the dimmed page or Escape puts it away.
entries.summary: The touch bottom sheet's frame: backdrop, slide-up, safe area and the modal layer (UX-14).
details: Built on Modal, so it is a named modal dialog: Escape and a press on the dimmed page close it, the page behind is inert, and focus goes back to what opened it. The backdrop is black at 40% and fades in; the column of cards rises from below the screen's edge (animate-sheet-in) and leaves as it came.

Where it sits is theme.css's .bottom-sheet: 8 px from the sides and the bottom, plus the home indicator's inset. Its cards take sheetCard (surface-float, rounded-2xl), drawn solid inside a sheet: frosted over the dimmed page, White's turned grey enough that a red Delete in the message sheet read at 4.2:1.
SHEET_QUERY, (hover: none) and (max-width: 760px), is where a sheet is wanted, and wantsSheet() reads it. A phone held sideways, 844 px wide, is wider than that, so a menu there stays a dropdown.

Menu draws its touch sheet in one, for the message actions, a conversation's row, the conversation's ⋯ and the account menu from the phone's You. Focus handling stays Menu's and Modal's: the menu's one trigger button is where focus goes back to.

entries.plain: The small hint that appears over a button when you point at it or reach it with the keyboard.
entries.summary: Explains compact controls without taking focus or blocking the page.
details: Hover opens after a short delay; keyboard focus opens immediately; Escape dismisses the hint. On the control that has focus, the first Escape dismisses only the hint, as in a dialog; a hint the pointer opened on another control goes, and the key carries on to wherever focus is. The floating portal follows its trigger and flips when needed.
Composes event handlers, accessible descriptions and refs, including React ref-cleanup behavior, so decorating a control does not replace its own lifetime contract.
The first hint waits 400 ms. Once one is showing, or has just gone, the next waits only 80 ms and slides over from where the last one was instead of growing in again. Hiding is immediate.

The floating text itself is TooltipBubble, out of the first download: loadTooltipBubble fetches it as the workspace opens or a hint is first wanted, and a hint opened before it arrives is drawn once it has.

disabled keeps the hint away and puts away one that is up, timers and all; Menu sets it on its button while the menu is open. Focus given back by a closing menu or dialog brings no hint, since React delivers no focus events while it commits; the pointer still resting on the button brings one after the usual wait.

entries.plain: Draws a hint's text beside its button and keeps it there as the page scrolls. It downloads in the background, so the app opens a little faster.
entries.summary: An open tooltip's floating text: placement, follow-on slide, Escape and window blur.
details: Placed in a portal on the trigger's dialog, main, nav or aside, or the fullscreen element holding it; flips sides when the preferred one does not fit, and follows its trigger on scroll, resize and every frame.

Escape closes it. Only while its trigger has focus does it keep that Escape from everything else. A hint opened by the pointer elsewhere used to hold it too: the phone drawer slides in under the pointer that opened it, onto the rail of workspaces, and that rail's hint kept Escape from closing the drawer while focus was on Jump to…

Split from Tooltip to make room for slice 7's status that clears itself, when the desktop entry stood at 499.2 kB of a 500 kB limit (since raised to 700 kB by #301): about 2.9 kB less for every first download.

entries.plain: Asks you to confirm before something that cannot be undone, and only goes ahead if you pick the named action.
entries.summary: Asks named questions for irreversible user actions and returns a boolean answer.
details: ConfirmProvider and useConfirm expose a promise resolved true only by the explicitly named action; cancellation, closing and Escape resolve false.
A destructive question begins on Cancel and can explain the consequence. Callers act on the answer rather than inferring permission from dismissal.
useOptionalConfirm is useConfirm where a screen may be drawn without a provider, as the sidebar is in tests: then nobody is asked.

entries.plain: The small notices that say whether something worked, where failures stay until you dismiss them and may offer Retry or Undo.
entries.summary: Reports operation outcomes without interrupting current input.
details: Success notices and heads-ups clear after a reading interval, while failures remain for acknowledgement and can offer an operation-specific retry or undo. A heads-up (kind info) has a ringed i and is read out politely, as a success is (E13b).
A bounded stack pauses countdowns during hover/focus and preserves a nearby focus destination when a notice is removed. Notices never make the workspace inert.

A notice rises in out of a slight blur. One dismissed by pointer or by its timer fades as its row folds away, so the notices after it slide up; one closed from the keyboard goes at once, so focus can move to its neighbour.

entries.plain: Small pieces that make changes visible: a count that pops in and rolls when it changes, words or an icon that swap in place, and a panel that steps in from the side.
entries.summary: Shared change-driven motion: badges, in-place swaps and stepped panels.
details: useChanges counts how often a value has changed since the component was first drawn, so what was already on screen when it opened stays still and only later changes move.

CountBadge is drawn as nothing at zero and pops in when it appears; its number rolls up when it changes, and above max it says 99+ for 99. Badge draws every count that says something waits on top of it; a reaction's count and the workspace rail's still use it directly. Swap regrows an icon, or raises words, out of a blur when what it shows changes. stepIn brings a new page in from the side it is on.
All of it follows the motion tokens in theme.css, and none of it plays for anyone who asked for less motion.

entries.plain: The small red number or dot that says something is waiting for you, such as unread mentions, drawn the same way everywhere.
entries.summary: Count and dot badges for unread and mentions, in one place (UX-14).
details: Two tones: quiet (a pale pill, semibold, for what is merely unread) and mention (Discord's red, bold, with its glow, badge-mention in theme.css). Two sizes: regular, 18 px, beside a row's name, and small, 16 px, on the corner of an icon. dot says only that there is something; max caps the number, as 99+.

Nothing is drawn at 0 or false. Built on CountBadge, it pops in when it comes and its number rolls; one there when the screen was drawn is still. Callers place it, and give it the ring that sets it apart from an icon, through className.

label is what it says in words, read in its place as an img: "2 unread mentions in general". Without one it is aria-hidden, for a badge whose control says it already, in its name (Friends, 1 new) or its description (the phone bar's).

It draws the sidebar's Activity and Threads counts, a channel's mention count and the header buttons' dots, the Direct messages panel's counts, dots and Friends dot, the phone bar's counts and dots, and the drawer button's. The rail's workspace badge is not moved yet; Activity's unread mark and the sidebar's unread nub are row markers, and the Threads panel's "3 new replies" is words, so neither is a badge.

entries.plain: What a list or panel with nothing in it says: what it is for and how to fill it, sometimes with a picture above and one thing to do.
entries.summary: The empty state, with a mark or without, and its one action (UX-14).
details: With an icon, a glowing tile (empty-tile in theme.css) above words in ink-dim, for a side panel or a dialog's list. Without, the words alone in ink-faint, centred, for a list inside a larger view. action adds one button under them, such as Clear the filter.

ListStatus draws its empty case with it, inside its status region, and puts EmptyAction outside that region, so what is read out as the list changes is the words alone and focus has somewhere to go when the action is replaced.

Lists already on screen and filtered to nothing draw one themselves: Browse channels, the people in New message (now after the list rather than inside it, which holds only its people), Friends and Recent searches. Screen share's picker keeps its own taller empty line, which holds the dialog's height steady, and Keyboard shortcuts keeps its live line.

entries.plain: Gives every list the same look while it is loading, refreshing, empty or offering to try again.
entries.summary: Keeps loading, refresh, empty and retry state consistent across lists.
details: Before first content it renders varied stand-in rows; later refreshes keep the current list and show a status line.

A stable live region and layout cleanup preserve focus when a Retry/empty-state action is replaced by results. This is a shared usability primitive rather than each panel inventing its own state layout.
Its empty case is an EmptyState, with the list's emptyIcon when it has one, and the empty list's action an EmptyAction kept outside the status region.

entries.plain: The end of a long list. It loads the next part as you scroll near it, and is also a Show more button for keyboards.
entries.summary: End-of-list control that loads the next page when it comes into view (UX-08).
details: An IntersectionObserver rooted in the panel's scroller asks for the next page a little before the end is visible, and is made again after each page, so a short list keeps filling until it fills the panel or ends.
It stays one button while loading (aria-disabled, not disabled) so focus is not lost, says when more could not load with Try again, and hands focus to its own wrapper when the list ends.

entries.plain: Catches a part of the screen that breaks and offers to retry it, without losing your connection or what you typed.
entries.summary: Contains a broken React view while preserving the workspace connection and typed work.
details: Catches render failures and supplies recoverable fallback controls at the relevant boundary.
Dismissal can retry the same tree without automatically reloading the whole app, allowing the live client and unsent state outside that boundary to remain owned.

entries.plain: Shows a loading message while a panel or dialog downloads on first use, and offers to close or reload if that fails.
entries.summary: Wraps on-demand panels and dialogs with loading and failed-chunk recovery.
details: Suspense announces what is loading and retains a way to close the pending view.
An ErrorBoundary confines a failed download to that view and provides close/reload actions, allowing the rest of the workspace to remain usable.

entries.plain: A page for people building OwnBase that shows every shared control in its states, in the dark and the light theme. Only the development version has it.
